articles.title: No wildlife board nod, stop-work order issued to Adani company’s power project in Satara
articles.summary: Satara DCF orders Adani Renewable Energy to halt 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage work for lack of NBWL clearance; seeks tree-felling approvals and project papers.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The deputy conservator of forests (DCF), Satara forest division, has issued a stop-work order to the project manager of Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd, Mumbai, for starting work on the 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project in the district’s Patan taluka without prior approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).Adani Group said the proposal for wildlife clearance has been submitted to the board.The action by DCF Amol Satpute came after it was separately flagged in Oct that Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL), which is executing the project, had understated the project cost to the state govt, slashing it from Rs 5,675 crore to Rs 56.75 crore, to reduce its statutory environmental obligations.Issuing a show-cause notice on Nov 13 under Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Maharashtra Tree Felling (Regulation) Act, 1964, the DCF sought a written explanation on the authority under which the project was initiated without the valid NBWL permission. He warned that if work continues at the site, strict legal and penal action would be initiated under the applicable forest laws.The notice asks whether permissions were obtained from the competent authorities for tree felling linked to the project. The company has been asked to submit the total number of trees approved for felling if such permissions exist, along with original or attested permits, and provide all related statutory approvals and project maps within the stipulated period.The reply was to be submitted to the range forest officer’s office within three days of receipt of the notice.An AGEL spokesperson said the necessary permissions/NOCs on land use and statutory requirements had been obtained from the competent authorities. The spokesperson said based on the environmental clearance granted in Feb 2025, Maharashtra Pollution Control Board issued the consent to establish on April 7, 2025 to allow the work to begin. “Construction activities commenced only after obtaining all the requisite approvals from the authorities concerned.”The company said the process for wildlife clearance has been duly initiated and pursued as part of the environmental clearance compliance process. “The proposal for survey and investigation activities was submitted in Jan 2025 and subsequently recommended by the state board for wildlife. The proposal for the project has since been submitted to NBWL and is currently under consideration. The project is being developed in full compliance with applicable statutory requirements and the directions of the competent authorities.”The spokesperson said no project component falls in any notified protected area or forest land, and that the NOC stating this was received on Jan 23, 2024.On Oct 30, Satara’s honorary wildlife warden Rohan Bhate had flagged an alleged discrepancy in the project cost declared to the state govt, stating it was shown as Rs 56.75 crore instead of Rs 5,675 crore. In representations to NBWL, the ministry of environment, forest and climate change (MoEFCC) and the CM, he sought an independent inquiry, arguing that an understated cost could amount to misrepresentation and could affect wildlife conservation contributions linked to the project value.MoEFCC’s environmental clearance issued on Feb 11, 2025, records the project cost at Rs 5,675 crore. It also lists Rs 39.3 crore as capital cost for the environment management plan and pollution control measures, and Rs 27.5 crore as recurring operation and maintenance cost.Reports also state that on Sept 7, AGEL chief operating officer Naresh Telugu submitted a letter to the principal chief conservator of forests (wildlife), Maharashtra, along with a notarised undertaking on a Rs 500-stamp paper, citing the project cost as Rs 56.75 crore. The undertaking reportedly said the figure was based on an “analogous estimation” used while submitting “Part IV,” requested authorities to consider Rs 56.75 crore as the project cost, and committed to mitigation and conservation measures.The company denied allegations of cost understatement to reduce statutory obligations, saying figures mentioned in the online forest and wildlife clearance proposal related only to preliminary investigations and surveys.In his letters, Bhate had said, “The difference between the estimated total project cost reflected in the available project documents and the amount stated in the notarised undertaking by AGEL is substantial. The two figures differ by a factor of 100. The administration of Sahyadri tiger reserve (STR) had communicated to AGEL well in advance that an amount equivalent to 4% of the total project cost, ie, approximately Rs 227 crore, was required to be deposited in the account of the STR Conservation Foundation for wildlife conservation and protection, subject to the applicable provisions and conditions.” He said based on the revised project cost of Rs 56.75 crore, an amount equivalent to 1% was calculated as Rs 56.75 lakh for payment. The remaining 3% was to be paid after NBWL’s clearance.“If the project cost has indeed been deliberately understated in the undertaking submitted to the state govt, the matter raises serious concerns regarding the possible misrepresentation of material financial information to govt and its consequential impact on the financial contribution required for wildlife conservation. Hence, it has been necessary to establish whether the project cost was correctly assessed, whether the applicable contribution requirements were properly implemented, and whether the decision to calculate the contribution on the basis of Rs 56.75 crore as revised project cost was supported by the relevant rules, official records and approved conditions,” Bhate had said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.standfirst: O Escritório de Excelência Operacional da cooperativa vem implantando projetos de melhoria contínua e revolucionando principais setores operacionais.
articles.summary:
O Escritório de Excelência Operacional da cooperativa vem implantando projetos de
melhoria contínua e revolucionando principais setores operacionais.
articles.body:
Durante recente encontro o Escritório de Excelência Operacional apresentou sete novos projetos. — Foto: Carlos Laerte

A implantação de 12 novos projetos de melhoria contínua em setores, a exemplo da recepção dos hospitais, laboratório, almoxarifado, na farmácia e no serviço de nutrição. Este é o principal balanço do Escritório de Excelência Operacional, que foi criado há 2 anos pela Unimed Vale do São Francisco, para melhorar os processos e entrega dos serviços, diminuir desperdícios e economizar o tempo e recursos nas operações.

Alicerçado e baseado na metodologia Lean Six Sigma, o Escritório começou com a implementação do curso Green Belt e a certificação de 25 colaboradores. Na ocasião, foram apresentados cinco trabalhos, que segundo a diretoria da cooperativa médica, geraram uma economia em torno de R$ 2 milhões.

Além de capacitação, suporte e treinamento das equipes, o Escritório de Excelência Operacional da Unimed Vale do São Francisco, atua como uma estrutura organizacional voltada para o gerenciamento de projetos da cooperativa. Com foco em resultados, gestão, metodologia, cultura e processos, seu papel principal é garantir que os projetos estejam alinhados aos objetivos institucionais.

Hoje, com lideranças certificadas em níveis Green, Black Belt, Master Black Belt, o Escritório ensina e capacita os colaboradores para que possam desenvolver projetos dentro das suas áreas de atuação, trazendo a melhoria contínua.

De acordo com a coordenadora do Escritório de Excelência Operacional, Cinthia Teles, a cooperativa vem obtendo resultados surpreendentes, a exemplo da economia de recursos, melhoria de performance nos setores e nos serviços.

“Estamos sempre revisitando nossos processos na busca por melhoria. Redução de desperdícios com tempo, com materiais e demais recursos deve ser uma prática contínua na busca por resultados que impactam diretamente na qualidade dos nossos serviços e consequentemente na experiência dos nossos clientes, cooperados e colaboradores”, ressaltou.

articles.title: US government proposes new rules for Green Cards; tells companies: American Workers are the best in the world, rule change will ensure they are …
articles.summary: The US government is proposing stricter rules for companies sponsoring foreign workers for employment-based Green Cards.
articles.body: The US government is proposing stricter rules for companies sponsoring foreign workers for employment-based Green Cards. The US Department of Labor says the changes will ensure that qualified American workers get the first opportunity to apply for high-skilled, high-paying jobs before companies turn to foreign workers. “American Workers are the best in the world, and they deserve the first and best job opportunities,” Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said while announcing the proposal. He added that the rule change would put American workers “first in line” for such jobs.The proposal seeks to overhaul the Permanent Labor Certification programme, also known as PERM. It is the first major update to the programme in nearly 20 years.For the unaware, PERM is an important step for many employment-based Green Card applications under the EB-2 and EB-3 categories. Before sponsoring a foreign worker for permanent employment, companies generally have to show that they could not find qualified US workers for the position and that hiring the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of American workers. PERM approval itself does not grant a Green Card.What changes are being proposed to Green Card rulesOne of the biggest changes involves how companies advertise jobs. The Labor Department wants employers to move away from print-based advertisements and use modern recruitment methods. Under the proposal, companies would have to advertise vacancies through their websites, online job portals and social media platforms. They may also use job fairs and campus recruitment.Employers would have to keep job advertisements open for at least 90 calendar days. If they normally advertise similar positions for a longer period, they would have to follow that longer period. The department says this would give qualified American workers more time to learn about vacancies and apply.The proposal would also require companies to use the same recruitment channels and methods for PERM positions that they use for similar jobs that do not require labour certification. Employers would have to make genuine efforts to consider qualified US applicants and provide job-related reasons if they reject them.Companies that laid off US workers could face restrictionsThe proposed rules also target companies that lay off American employees while seeking to sponsor foreign workers. Under the proposal, employers would be barred from filing a PERM application if they had laid off US workers in the same or a similar occupation at the relevant work location during the previous two years.If a company lays off American workers after filing a PERM application, it would have to consider potentially qualified laid-off employees for the position. This requirement could continue until the related Form I-140 immigrant petition is approved or the case reaches a final decision.Employers would also have to inform the Labor Department, and the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) where applicable, about such layoffs within five business days.Nurses and physical therapists could also face new requirementsThe Labor Department has proposed ending the administrative exemptions under a system known as Schedule A. At present, certain occupations, including professional nurses and physical therapists, can bypass the usual labour market test under Schedule A. The exemption also covers certain individuals with exceptional ability in the sciences, arts and performing arts.If the proposal is adopted, employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers in these categories would also have to test the US labour market and consider qualified American applicants.When will the proposed Green Card rules take effectThe changes are not final yet. The Labor Department has invited the public to submit comments on the proposal for 60 days after its publication in the Federal Register on November 17.The proposal is part of the US administration's wider efforts to tighten employer-sponsored immigration pathways and strengthen protections for American workers. If finalised, the changes could make the PERM process more demanding for companies seeking to sponsor foreign employees for permanent residency in the US.Your child uses AI every day. articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers got some unfortunate news following a 20-point defeat to the Minnesota Vikings. The post Packers Get Crushing Report After Bad Loss to...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are two games above .500 heading into their bye week, which should put them in a highly favorable position with regards to playoff contention come the end of the regular season, but the oddities of the NFC North in 2026 have rendered the opposite true.

Social media-based salary cap specialist Ken Ingalls, who focuses almost exclusively on the Packers, recently laid out the math on Green Bay's postseason chances — and the numbers are not good.

Everything went wrong for the Packers' playoff chances yesterday. Lions, Vikings, Rams, Seahawks win. Packers lose. Chance to make the playoffs dropped to 35%. Week 12 against the Rams is their largest impact game remaining on the schedule. 58% with a win / 23% with a loss.

Week 12 against the Rams is their largest impact game remaining on the schedule. 58% with a win / 23% with a loss.

Packers Desperately Need Pass-Rusher Micah Parsons to Return to Action in Los Angeles

Those implications for Green Bay's Thanksgiving Eve contest against the Rams in Los Angeles make the injury status of pass-rusher Micah Parsons all the more critical to the Packers' chances of success, not only in moving to 7-4 on the season but of keeping their playoff hopes above water.

Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed in an interview session on Monday that the team intends to bring Parsons back into an on-field role against the Rams on November 25. But he also said the superstar outside linebacker isn't quite there yet.

"We'll see," LaFleur said of Parsons playing nine days from now. "There's still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before I think we can definitively say that he's a go. But he's been showing progress, and we'll see where he's at by the end of the week."

Parsons spoke with reporters earlier this month and was also unwilling to put a definitive stamp on his return timeline, saying he did not want to put more pressure on it than necessary or make a promise about playing that he was not sure he could keep.

Packers Face Scary Rams' Defensive Front After Bye Week

Parsons' return would undoubtedly prove an enormous boost to the Packers' entire team. But that said, it was not the defense that was the problem against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

Minnesota rolled the Packers in Green Bay by 20 points (30-10), but the true culprit was the Packers' four turnovers, and those were a direct result of the offensive line's inability to protect quarterback Jordan Love.

While it is true that the Vikings defense is the fiercest and most relentless unit in the entire NFL with regards to QB pressure, Minnesota leads the league with 37 sacks through Week 10, Green Bay was also woefully unprepared to stop its opponent in that regard.

The Packers have a week and a half to figure out the situation up front, as the likes of Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and several other elite-level defensive linemen who wear Rams uniforms will be waiting for them at SoFi Stadium just ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

articles.title: WTGL: Motor City Golf Club win first overtime match in tournament's history vs Lottie Woad's Boston Common Golf
articles.summary: Motor City Golf Club secure 7-6 overtime victory over Boston Common Golf in dramatc WTGL victory - the first ever to go to overtime; England's Lottie Woad part of beaten side, but chipped in sensationally to force overtime session; Albane Valenzuela then beat Woad to clinch victory
articles.body:
Motor City are in full control at 2-0-0 but things weren't nearly as easy this time as they were for an 8-3 win over Los Angeles Golf Club in their opener.

Boston (0-0-1) overcame an early 3-0 deficit and never stopped fighting in their debut match, earning one point in the standings for the overtime loss.

Detroit hasn't wasted any time getting acclimated around SoFi Center. The new team has already put up 15 points in their first two matches and proved itself as a serious contender on Monday with Lexi Thompson, Jeeno Thitikul and Valenzuela staying poised when Boston rallied down the stretch.

They also have plenty of confidence and a firm grasp of strategy, throwing the Hammer before players teed off at No 14 and leaning on world No 2 Thitikul to deliver. She did just that, winning the hole to earn two points and give Detroit a 6-4 advantage amid a wild singles session.

Boston had the advantage off the tee at the par-three third and threw the Hammer looking for a quick 2-0 lead. When Lexi Thompson made a 30-foot birdie putt and raised her putter in celebration, Detroit threw a Hammer of their own and Khang's nine-footer didn't fall as MCGC took a 3-0 lead for a big momentum swing.

It was the perfect example of how quickly things can change in WTGL with this format, and a sign of things to come later in the match.

Woad, who came out with an homage to her home country sporting a Leeds United Premier League jersey, was part of a Boston side who put forth an outstanding effort in their first go-round at SoFi Center.

Boston and Motor City were still scoreless entering the par-three third, where Thompson rolled in a 30-footer for birdie and gave Motor City a 3-0 lead with two Hammers in play.

Khang cut into the lead at the next, nailing a seven-foot birdie putt to make it 3-1. But MCGC continued to pour it on with a 19-foot birdie make from Valenzuela at No 5, giving her team a 4-1 advantage.

Boston continued to fight back and keep the match within reach, earning another point at the sixth on an eight-foot birdie make from Iwai to cut the deficit to two. Iwai came through with the flatstick again at No 9, rolling a perfect lag putt from 63 feet for a conceded birdie to make it 4-3 Motor City entering singles.

With the deficit down to one, Khang stepped up and made birdie at No 10 to best Thompson and tie the match at 4-4.

Iwai and Thitikul traded birdies at the 11th with impressive up-and-downs as the intensity continued to build down the stretch. Things continued to ramp up at the 12th, where Valenzuela drained a 25-footer for birdie to match Woad and keep it tied as Detroit and Boston continued to go shot-for-shot.

Thompson and Khang traded pars at the 13th and Detroit threw the Hammer before players teed off at the 14th, meaning Iwai had to accept. That showed how much confidence MCGC has in Thitikul and she delivered with a beautiful pin-high tee shot while Iwai's tee ball bounced off the bridge of The Last Toll and into the penalty area.

Boston eventually conceded the hole and Detroit regained the lead, 6-4.

Boston threw a Hammer at the last, needing to win two points to stay alive. Needing to get up-and-down from off the green to have a chance, Woad instead chipped in to win the hole and send the match to overtime in spectacular fashion.

Thompson hit it inside nine feet to start the best-of-three, closest-to-the-pin overtime session, giving Motor City the early advantage.

Khang narrowly inched out Thitikul in the second round as the match came down to the final shots.

Valenzuela came through for Detroit in the end, besting Woad to cap an epic victory for MCGC that could have gone either way down the stretch.

The WTGL follows on from the success of the Tomorrow's Golf League (TGL), founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy's TMRW Sports, in partnership with the PGA Tour.

The women's edition of the tech-infused golf league will see LPGA Tour stars feature in a unique team format, with five teams (representing five different cities) of five-player rosters confirmed for the inaugural season.

The season-long competition takes place across November and December at the SoFi Center in Florida, a purpose-built indoor venue, with every shot live and all the players mic'd up for the made-for-TV format.

Both the 2026 and 2027 editions of WTGL will be broadcast exclusively on Sky Sports as part of an expansion of its golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi.

articles.title: PGA Tour: Chad Ramey saves tour card with rain-delayed Austin Championship title win
articles.summary: USA's Chad Ramey after Austin Championship title success saves PGA Tour card and grants two-year exemption: "My life went from very uncertain of what I'm going to be doing in January to now knowing what I'm doing the next two years. You can't write it up any better"
articles.body:
Ramey won for the second time in his career, the other coming in 2022 at an opposite-field event in the Dominican Republic.

This one was far more significant because Ramey was at No 136 in the FedEx Cup with two tournaments remaining.

The win puts him in the upper-tier Championship Series with $20m purses in 2028 when the tour's new competition model begins.

"First and foremost, I'm just relieved," Ramey said. "I mean, coming into this week, I was battling for my job.

"To come out on top and have a win, a two-year exemption, my life went from very uncertain of what I'm going to be doing in January to now knowing what I'm doing the next two years.

"It's unbelievable. It seems like for whatever reason I play my best golf when my back is against the wall. It's very rewarding. I'm very thankful.

"My game has been so close for so long. I just haven't quite got over the hump. All the way through the bag, I played very well and the putter got hot."

Ramey was in the lead, but never comfortably. Hayden Springer made a quick surge early on the back nine with a birdie-eagle-birdie stretch, the eagle coming at No 13 with a wedge from 117 yards on the side of a hill.

Ramey began to seize control with a 12-foot birdie on the 11th, a 10-foot birdie on the 13th and then a two-putt birdie on the par-five 14th to take him to 19 under, giving him a three-shot lead until Kohles closed the gap late.

Kohles made a late surge after a 15-foot birdie putt on the par-5 18th put him one shot behind at 66. Ramey was steady as ever on the closing hole at Omni Barton Creek, laying up and hitting wedge to just inside 10 feet for a final birdie that put him at 20 under.

It was the first time a full final round was held on Monday since The Players Championship in 2022.

"I was not calm at all, especially having to sit at the hotel all day Sunday, watch it rain," Ramey added.

"That was miserable. I'd much rather be out here playing golf. But like I said earlier, I came into today just telling myself just mentally stay aggressive. You know, just don't let up, just stay aggressive.

"You can't write it up any better. My dad and my wife were there for the first win in Puntacana, and for them to be here along with my son for my second win, just can't write it any better."

articles.title: Hundreds attend meeting about huge data centre near Kings Lynn
articles.summary: The developers, Evolution Power Limited, say its two sites will make an important contribution towards the UK building a "cleaner, lower cost and more secure energy system".
articles.body:
Hundreds of people attended an extraordinary council meeting to discuss plans for a huge new data centre and one of the UK's largest solar farms near King's Lynn in Norfolk.

The Longmarsh Green Energy (LGE) project would cover 4,695 acres (1,900 hectares) of farmland across two sites south of King's Lynn in Norfolk.

About 350 people attended the meeting at King's Lynn and West Norfolk Borough Council, with about 200 of those watching via a live stream in King's Lynn Minster.

A spokesperson for Longmarsh said the project would "make an important contribution" to energy systems and supporting online networks.

Members of the public raised concerns including the loss of agricultural land and food security.

Questions were also raised over why prime farmland would be used instead of brownfield sites.

Natural England, a public body which advises the government, classifies the affected area as grade one - meaning it is "excellent quality agricultural land".

Because of its scale, it will be deemed a nationally significant infrastructure project (NSIP), which means final say will rest with the government rather than the local authority.

The council voted unanimously to recommend five points including writing to the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero, asking for local communities to "be at the heart" of planning decisions.

It also recommended working with other local authorities in responding to NSIPs in West Norfolk, to oppose renewable energy developments, where appropriate, that lack support and threaten farmland.

The council also recommended a review of energy distribution and infrastructure and to evaluate any final government decisions and to pursue legal challenges if warranted.

A spokesperson for Longmarsh Green Energy Consultation said: "Longmarsh Green Energy will make an important contribution to helping the UK build a cleaner, lower cost and more secure energy system as well as supporting the online networks we all rely on - from emails, banking and streaming services to national defence and our NHS records.

"We recognise the importance of local community input into the design of our proposals and are currently consulting on the project prior to submitting a Development Consent Order application."

A public consultation is open via the project's website until 26 November. An application is due to be submitted by April 2027.

It could take six months for the plans to be examined by the Planning Inspectorate. A decision could be made by July 2028.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour following LIV Golf collapse
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau agrees to join the DP World Tour for next season.
articles.body:
Two-time US Open champion Bryson DeChambeau has agreed to join the DP World Tour for next season.

DeChambeau was among a host of star names who joined LIV Golf four years ago and maintained his commitment even after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing for the breakaway tour in April.

Earlier this month the 33-year-old American said he "gave everything" to keep LIV Golf alive as the tour confirmed its intention to wind down operations.

As first reported in the Telegraph, , external DeChambeau successfully submitted his application to join the European Tour before Sunday's deadline.

DeChambeau has already confirmed he will compete in Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge - a DP World Tour event - in South Africa in December.

As a recent major champion DeChambeau has been given 'category one' membership by the DP World Tour, which means he is guaranteed entry to any event across the season.

Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson - other former major champions who defected to LIV - have signed agreements to receive invitations to a specific number of tournaments.

"There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months," said DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings.

"As golf's global tour, we have taken a pragmatic approach to this unique and unprecedented situation as we go into next year, always with the best interests of our entire membership at the forefront of our minds.

"We realise there are different viewpoints but this approach, discussed and agreed with our tournament committee and allied to this responsibly managed programme of invites, will add value which, in turn, will benefit the tour as a whole."

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau: Former major champion takes DP World Tour membership for 2027 season after LIV Golf's collapse
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau has taken Category One membership on the DP World Tour; Ex-major champions Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson among LIV Golfers to have signed agreements to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments for the 2027 season
articles.body:
The two-time US Open winner's future was uncertain after LIV Golf confirmed they would wind down operations earlier this month, but DeChambeau has now taken an automatic exemption to play full-time on the DP World Tour.

DeChambeau applied for membership before the November 15 deadline and has been given Category One status - the highest-priority category - as the 2024 US Open champion, enabling him to play any DP World Tour event he chooses.

LIV Golf players are currently ineligible on the PGA Tour for at least 12 months from their last start in the breakaway league, leaving DeChambeau among the high-profile players now using the DP World Tour as a way back onto the established tours.

Membership categories for the 2027 DP World Tour season were announced Tuesday, with former major champion Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson among ex-LIV golf players signing agreements to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments next season.

Abraham Ancer, Lucas Herbert, Michael La Sasso, Joaquin Niemann, Carlos Ortiz and Thomas Pieters also signed similar deals, which exclude Rolex Series tournaments and include designated events for each player where they would "add value".

"Our 2027 season is set to be one of the most keenly contested campaigns in our 55-year history," said DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings. "There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months.

"As golf's global Tour, we have taken a pragmatic approach to this unique and unprecedented situation as we go into next year, always with the best interests of our entire membership at the forefront of our minds.

"We realise there are different viewpoints but this approach, discussed and agreed with our Tournament Committee and allied to this responsibly managed programme of invites, will add value which, in turn, will benefit the Tour as a whole."

The 2027 campaign was the final opportunity for DeChambeau to join the DP World Tour via his major victory, as every season the membership was not activated reduced the five-year window by 12 months.

Speaking on the possibility of DeChambeau featuring on the DP World Tour, Rory McIlroy said earlier this month: "I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments."

DeChambeau previously said LIV Golf would 'exist forever' and confirmed he still believes team golf is 'essential to growing the game', with the nine-time PGA Tour winner now set to return to action at the Nedbank Golf Challenge from December 3-6 - live on Sky Sports .

The DP World Tour insist invites across the season have been carefully managed by their Player Relations Department, following extensive modelling to 'ensure and preserve playing opportunities for existing members'.

Former Ryder Cup stars Lee Westwood, Sergio Garcia, Henrik Stenson, Martin Kaymer, Paul Casey and Graeme McDowell - all ex LIV-Golf members - hold Category 11a membership via the DP World Tour's career money list.

Ian Poulter, Louis Oosthuizen, Charl Schwartzel and Branden Grace are former LIV Golf players in the next membership category via their career money earnings, with a full list of DP World Tour exemption categories available here .

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau to join European tour for 2027 season after demise of LIV Golf
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau will play on the European tour for the 2027 season following the demise of LIV Golf.DeChambeau has taken Category 1 status, the tour said T...
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau will play on the European tour for the 2027 season following the demise of LIV Golf .

DeChambeau has taken Category 1 status, the tour said Tuesday, referring to its highest priority ranking, meaning the American can play in whichever tournament he chooses.

DeChambeau had the option to join the European tour because he won a major — the 2024 U.S. Open — in the last five years.

He was previously a star on LIV, which announced two weeks ago in bankruptcy court it plans to wind down operations instead of launching a new version after losing the financial support of Saudi Arabia.

Before moving to the LIV circuit, DeChambeau was on the PGA Tour, which typically has a one-year ban of players dating to their most recent LIV appearance.

On Monday, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said his board had "thoughtful discussions" about the future of players at LIV Golf, adding: "I hope to have more to say in the beginning of the new year."

The addition of DeChambeau, who has his own YouTube channel with more than 3 million subscribers, is a huge boon to the European tour.

It comes after Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton — the winners of the last two events of the 2026 season — announced they will be returning to the tour after their departure from LIV, along with Sergio Garcia .

In a statement announcing its membership categories for 2027, the European tour said nine players coming off LIV — including Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith — had signed agreements to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments next season.

The other players were Abraham Ancer, Lucas Herbert, Michael La Sasso, Joaquin Niemann, Carlos Ortiz and Thomas Pieters.

articles.title: PGA Tour confirm 'no plans' for returning route for LIV Golf players as Tiger Woods backs big changes to tour's structure
articles.summary: The PGA Tour board engaged in "thoughtful discussions" about the future of players at LIV Golf without confirming a pathway back; Brian Rolapp discussed LIV Golf players' future during an announcement on the PGA Tour structure from 2028
articles.body:
LIV Golf confirmed earlier this month they were winding down operations instead of launching a new version, because of a lack of financial support, leaving players looking for pathways back to traditional tours.

Brooks Koepka took financial penalties earlier this year to return to the PGA Tour via the Returning Member Program, a pathway created for a limited group of 'elite performers', with Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith elected not to follow suit.

Rahm has said he 'probably would do it' if offered a similar route back again, while DeChambeau said he would go about 'whatever is next the right way' and has since accepted DP World Tour membership , although Rolapp has played down that - as things stand - being a possibility next season.

"There are no plans for that currently, no," Rolapp told reporters on a media call, following the PGA Tour approving details for its new ​competitive structure from 2028.

Players are currently suspended for 12 months from their last LIV Golf appearance before being eligible to feature on the PGA Tour, with Patrick Reed being a full-time member on the DP World Tour this season before heading back to the US circuit in 2027.

Sergio Garcia, Dustin Johnson and Joaquin Niemann are among the players following a similar schedule on the DP World Tour next season, with the PGA Tour having "thoughtful discussion" about how to incorporate LIV Golf players going forward.

"We have heard from ​our fans and we know that they want the best players playing ‌together and we share that view," Rolapp added. "I have said that from day one when I took the job, I am interested in doing whatever makes the PGA Tour better.

"I have said that from day one when I took the job, I am interested in doing whatever makes the PGA Tour better. As we have a membership organization, we have rules and, as I shared before, they exist to ensure fairness and competitive balance.

"Rules matter and they will be enforced. We engaged in thoughtful discussion on the topic of LIV players with both boards [PGA Tour and the PGA Tour Enterprises]. As far as we have read, bankruptcy proceedings are ongoing and the process is complex.

"I hope to have more to say in the beginning of the New Year but, until that time, I will not speculate on the outcome or individual decisions players make."

Tiger backs changes to PGA Tour structure

The Future Competition Committee - chaired by Tiger Woods - announced Monday further details of the PGA Tour's new competitive structure, set to debut in 2028.

"I can confidently say the PGA Tour is in the best position it has ever been," Woods said. "We created a competitive model grounded in meritocracy, built to last and that offers the best opportunity for the next generation of players."

The PGA Tour is doing away with the PGA Tour Americas, instead creating a vast network of feeder tournaments throughout the year that will have one ranking system.

The Korn Ferry Tour will have at least 20 tournaments with $1m purses (£756,000) and the leading 20 players will be promoted to the Challenger Series.

The top 20 players in the Challenger Series advance to the Championship Series, with the board approving elevating the final event that would be for the top 90 players.

The winner of the season finale would be promoted to the Championship Series, even if he isn't among the top 20. The number of places on the Championship Series via the DP World Tour's "Race to Dubai" rankings has yet to be finalised.

articles.title: ‘Hypocrite’ – Warriors fans have had enough of Draymond Green after what he just said
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors fans have officially reached their boiling point with Draymond Green following Monday night’s loss to the New Orleans Pelicans. Golden...
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors fans have officially reached their boiling point with Draymond Green following Monday night's loss to the New Orleans Pelicans.

Golden State fell to 8–6 on Monday night after getting destroyed 115–94 by the New Orleans Pelicans.

Dug into a 35–9 hole in the first quarter, the Warriors never had a chance as they dropped their third straight game without Stephen Curry. With their superstar sidelined, Golden State couldn't buy a bucket, shooting just 33.3% from the floor.

Draymond Green didn't do much to spark the offense either in 25 minutes of action, he finished with only 2 points on 1-of-3 shooting, adding 8 rebounds, 5 assists, a steal, and a block.

Draymond Green claims he's the 'leader' for the Warriors

Speaking to reporters after the loss, Draymond Green took the blame for Golden State's sluggish start following their previous blowout against San Antonio.

When asked why the Warriors came out so flat in New Orleans, Green pointed the finger straight at himself, saying, "Because I'm the leader. And I can't let us come out like that. So that's on me."

It's safe to say that Warriors fans weren't best pleased with the comments on X.

One fan started: "That's a funny thing to say after getting ejected already this season."

"That's on me! Yeah, you're dropping 2 points every game! Poole ain't lying, you're an expensive backpack." Another furious fan said.

Another agreed: "You are not the leader, bro."

"Do something about it then before we waste the last year of Steph's prime." Said another.

This supporter has had enough: "Enough is enough."

If Draymond Green is the leader setting the tone, Golden State is in real trouble. Just two weeks ago against Phoenix, he got ejected after throwing Khaman Maluach to the floor and grabbing Dillon Brooks by the neck, then picked up another flagrant foul against San Antonio days later.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau leads group of ex-LIV Golf players headed to DP World Tour
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau will play 2027 on the DP World Tour.
articles.body:
LIV Golf's loss is the DP World Tour's massive gain. Two-time U.S. Open winner and YouTube golfer extraordinaire Bryson DeChambeau will lead a notable contingent of ex-LIV players who will spend 2027 competing on the international tour.

DeChambeau, along with Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Dustin Johnson, Cam Smith and many other LIV players, strengthens the DP World Tour, serving as a sign that after five years, the broken golf world is healing.

LIV Golf, the Saudi Arabia-funded breakaway tour, is winding down after a plan to advance into a second phase fell apart because of a lack of player support . DeChambeau was the most notable question mark remaining from the league's dissolution; he could have, in theory, done anything up to and including a YouTube-and-majors career arc. But he has clearly opted, in a decision first reported by the Telegraph , for a more traditional tour arrangement.

The DP World Tour covers the entire globe, starting with the season-opening events in Australia later this month. From there, the Tour will head to South Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Europe, with stops for qualified players at the four majors.

One option not available to DeChambeau and the rest of the LIV players, at least for now, is a return to the PGA Tour. The Tour offered a onetime pathway back for notable LIV golfers such as DeChambeau and Rahm earlier this year, but only Brooks Koepka took advantage of that option. As a result, Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has reiterated on several occasions that a similar route back to the Tour is not presently available.

So DeChambeau, Rahm et al. could follow the route of Masters champion Patrick Reed, who left LIV after the 2025 season, played the entirety of 2026 on the DP World Tour, and clinched his PGA Tour card for next season over the past weekend.

Along with DeChambeau, Rahm and Hatton, nine former LIV players have agreed to a limited schedule: major winners Johnson, Smith and Bubba Watson, as well as Abraham Ancer, Lucas Herbert, Michael La Sasso, Joaquin Niemann, Carlos Ortiz and Thomas Pieters.

The return of LIV players will make the DP World Tour's 2027 one of the most talent-laden in the tour's history. The tour already includes Rory McIlroy, Matt Fitzpatrick, Shane Lowry, Adam Scott and Justin Rose, along with other former LIV players already in the fold such as Henrik Stenson, Graeme McDowell and Sergio Garcia.

articles.title: Hank Green is self-funding ClockwiseTV, a curated educational video platform for kids | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Alongside CEO Leslie Morgan, Hank Green set out to create the video platform he wished his kid had.
articles.body:
“I was recently on a podcast and the host asked me what my lowest part of my career was,” Hank Green mused on a recent episode of his own podcast, Dear Hank & John.

That’s a tough question for anyone to answer, let alone someone who has spent about two decades regularly posting videos online for an increasingly broad audience.

“Really the low — the long low — was just watching as [the internet] went from being this lovely thing that a bunch of creatives were goofing around [on] to it being freaking everything, and mattering so much, and getting taken over by all tons of terrible vibes and algorithms selecting for outrage, and it being a huge degradation to the social order,” Green said.

That’s bleak, but Green is at least trying to lead by example in showing that we don’t have to accept that the good parts of the internet are gone forever. The notoriously entrepreneurial vlogbrother has spun up a new company with Leslie Morgan : ClockwiseTV, a curated, ad-free educational video platform for children ages 8 to 12.

“[Hank] came to me last September like, ‘I have had this idea for a really long time, and it stems from the fact that my child, who’s nine, always is asking me for five more minutes on whatever device he’s on,’” Morgan, who has spent 20 years working on the business side of the creator economy, told TechCrunch. “I was like, I have that same problem… ‘How do you contain time, but also give the child agency?’”

Clockwise’s answer to that question seems to be this: At the start of each viewing session, the parent and child decide how long they can watch, and the platform will recommend videos that will adhere to that time frame. If a kid is in the midst of a 30-minute session and has already watched two 10-minute videos, they’re not going to be suggested a 20-minute video when they only have 10 minutes left.

The startup is addressing a pretty widespread concern among parents, who are worried about more than simply negotiating with their children about how long they can use the iPad. According to a 2025 study by the Pew Research Center, about 51% of parents of children 12 or younger say their kid watches YouTube every day, among other video apps.

YouTube has a dedicated app for children under 13, YouTube Kids, which offers a wide range of parental controls, but the app can reportedly still serve children a wealth of low-quality AI slop. Other apps that don’t have a kids’ version can be even worse.

Clockwise says it is also solving that problem by hand-curating a library of educational videos from creators like Odd Animal Specimens , Draw with Jazza , and Nerdforge , as well as channels Green had a hand in creating, like Crash Course Kids and SciShow Kids .

“When you go into the app, there’s a dozen choices [of videos] that you can choose from to start,” Morgan, the startup’s CEO, said. “There’s search functionality as well, so you can say, ‘Hey, I’m really interested in math today,’ so you can look up Stand-up Maths and look at what’s available in that time frame.”

Some of these creators cater to people of all ages, but Clockwise says its team manually reviews each video it uploads and edits it so that it’s ready for younger eyes. The team might remove anything from embedded product placement to what Morgan calls “spectacle power tool use.”

“ Simone Giertz , who’s a maker creator, tends to curse a lot. But a lot of that content is great for kids,” Morgan explains. “She makes a skateboard for her three-legged dog, and if she drops an f-bomb, we’re going to cut it out so that it’s suitable for children.”

Clockwise pays these creators an upfront fee to use their videos, then shares 25% of revenue based on watch time. Clockwise charges parents $6.99 per month or $69.99 per year to access the platform, which it promises will remain free of ads.

“Humans are checking [the videos] four times at least before it’s ever published into our app […] That will always stay,” Morgan said. “We’re not interested in using AI to wash down our content.”

So far, a few hundred parents have tested Clockwise with their children in beta. On Tuesday, the platform is opening to the public with apps made for iOS and Android smartphones and tablets.

The platform has not taken on any outside funding, and is funded by Green himself.

“It was really important that he had full control,” Morgan said. “He wanted to invest his own wealth into this. That was also really important because it is something he just believes in so wholeheartedly, as do I.”

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau's Future Revealed After LIV Golf Run, Receives 'Category 1 Status' on New Tour
articles.summary: Two-time U.S. Open champion Bryson DeChambeau is signing on with the DP World Tour for the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Two-time U.S. Open champion Bryson DeChambeau is signing on with the DP World Tour for the 2027 season.

The tour said Tuesday that DeChambeau received "Category 1" status, which is reserved for winners of the Race to Dubai or one of the four major tournaments since 2022.

DeChambeau was the biggest remaining domino following the collapse of LIV Golf, and nobody was sure what his next move would be.

The 33-year-old is one of golf's most recognizable stars, and he has built a sizable following online through his popular YouTube channel . He suggested in May that could be his primary focus if LIV ceased operations.

"I think, from my perspective, I'd love to grow my YouTube channel three times, maybe even more," DeChambeau said, per ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "I would love to. I'd love to do a bunch of dubbing in different languages, giving the world more reason to watch YouTube. And then I'd love to play tournaments that want me."

Earlier this month, he remained vague in a statement regarding his immediate future:

DeChambeau subsequently laid out plans to design a championship-level golf facility in Clovis, California, his hometown. Some wondered whether he was making a career pivot to his DeChambeau Designs venture.

Tuesday's announcement signals he's still looking to compete at the highest level, and that's what the DP World Tour offers him with his PGA Tour status still murky .

From a performance standpoint, few LIV Golf stars suffered more over time than DeChambeau. He missed the cut in the first three majors this year before tying for 14th in the Open Championship. He also went 1-3-1 at the 2025 Ryder Cup and halved his singles match with Matt Fitzpatrick.

By playing a regular DP World Tour schedule, DeChambeau can reaffirm his status as one of the top golfers in the game.

Even if he doesn't recapture his best form, his presence is another boost to the tour, which is benefiting in a big way from LIV's bankruptcy. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio Garcia, Joaquin Niemann, Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith are among the other LIV castoffs who have committed to the European circuit.

articles.title: Tiger Woods: 15-time major champion to make PGA Tour comeback at December's Hero World Challenge in Bahamas
articles.summary: Tiger Woods has been added a tournament invite for the Hero World Challenge from December 3-6, hosted by his foundation; Woods has not featured in a competitive event since 2024; watch Woods' latest comeback live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The invite-only tournament - hosted by Woods' foundation - has previously been used as a comeback event for Woods, who has played a limited schedule since suffering career-threatening injuries in a car crash in February 2021.

Woods has not appeared on the PGA Tour since missing the cut at The Open in July 2024, with the 15-time major champion missing the entire 2025 season after rupturing his Achilles tendon.

He underwent fresh back surgery last October and missed the 2026 campaign after "stepping away" from PGA Tour golf , following a car crash in March that saw him charged with reckless driving , but is now scheduled to return in Albany, Bahamas.

The 50-year-old is one of three sponsor's exemptions added to the field for the 20-man event, held from December 3-6, with 2019 US Open champion Gary Woodland and Rickie Fowler the others to be included.

Woods was a notable absentee from the initial line-up announcement last month, with Hideki Matsuyama returning as defending champion and Scottie Scheffler looking to win for a third time in four years, while Players champion Cameron Young and former US Open winner Matt Fitzpatrick also feature.

The former world No 1 is currently listed as 'unranked' in the OWGR standings, having only completed four 72-hole tournaments over the last six seasons and not had a worldwide top 10 since January 2020.

He last featured at the Hero World Challenge in 2023, his first appearance since withdrawing mid-tournament from The Masters earlier that year, although won the event in 2001, 2004, 2006, 2007 and 2011.

Woods was listed in Jupiter Links GC's expanded five-player roster for the 2026/27 TGL season, beginning December 27, with Kevin Kisner - replaced by Keith Mitchell in the line-up - expecting the five-time Masters champion to feature more frequently.

"I'm not on the team anymore," Kisner told the Fore Play Podcast last month. "I had a two-year contract with Jupiter Links. Tiger wants to play and they wanted to sign Keith Mitchell, which is totally fine with me.

"Rob [McNamara], ​Tiger's guy, he texted me a long text last week. Just telling me what they did on their decisions, how they were moving around and what players were going to do and that Tiger wanted to play a full schedule."

Woods previously described the PNC Championship as his "fifth major", with the 36-hole team competition seeing a former winner of a major or The Players tee it up alongside a family member.

He featured in every edition since 2020 with his son, Charlie Woods, who fired a hole-in-one during the 2024 contest before they lost in a play-off to Bernhard Langer's team, although missed last year's contest due to injury.

Team Woods have yet to confirm their entry into this year's edition, held from December 19-20 and also live on Sky Sports , although there are spaces for them still to be included in the line-up.

"He plays there [at the Hero World Challenge] and PNC [Championship]," Kisner predicted. "He's going to play both.

"Come back, get your feet wet at the Hero, play with Charlie [Woods] in the Father/Son, play some TGL, get ready for Augusta."

articles.title: Tiger Woods Returns for 2026 Hero World Challenge, Latest on Updated Field of Players
articles.summary: Fifteen-time major champion Tiger Woods is aiming for a return to full competition in the Hero World Challenge in December.
articles.body:
Fifteen-time major champion Tiger Woods is aiming for a return to full competition in the Hero World Challenge in December.

The tournament announced Tuesday that Woods is in the 20-player limited field, which includes Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Russell Henley, Matt Fitzpatrick and J.J. Spaun.

The golf legend is the host for the annual event in the Bahamas.

Woods hasn't entered a 72-hole tournament since the 2024 Open Championship. Accumulating injuries from his golf career on top of his serious car crash in 2021 have significantly curtailed his availability in recent years.

Any comeback plans for the 2026 season were shelved after he was arrested in March on suspicion of driving under the influence.

Fans did at least get to see Woods in a less rigorous setting this past spring. He represented Jupiter Links Golf Club in the TGL Finals.

There are no misconceptions about the state of Woods' game at this point. Between his age (50) and all of the injuries, he's unlikely to be a contender at a major tournament, and he'll never compete full time on the PGA Tour again.

Still, Woods might continue to move the needle more than anyone else in golf. The Hero World Challenge undoubtedly became more interesting with him in it. Fans will immediately get hopeful if he makes it through all four rounds and performs reasonably well.

Should that happen, perhaps he'll be healthy enough to enter the four majors on top of a notable PGA Tour event here and there in 2027. Don't write off a debut on the senior tour , either.

articles.title: Tiger Woods making return to competitive golf at December's Hero World Challenge
articles.summary: Woods has not played competitively since stepping away from golf following his rollover crash in March.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is making his return to competitive golf at next month's Hero World Challenge , it was announced on Tuesday.

The 15-time major champion will tee it up from Dec. 3-6 in the Bahamas, joining a 20-player field that includes Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Justin Thomas and Xander Schauffele, among others. Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland were also announced as additions on Tuesday.

The last official event Woods played was the 2024 Open Championship. The last time the 50-year-old Woods played competitive golf was in March during the TGL Final. Days later, he was involved in a rollover crash in Jupiter Island , Florida, and stepped away from golf to "seek treatment" at a rehab facility in Switzerland.

Woods ended up pleading guilty to misdemeanor charges of reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after his arrest. His driver's license was suspended for five years as a result.

Last week, Woods told Sirius XM PGA Tour Radio that he's "feeling better" and has been "training quite a bit." He added he would be attending the Hero World Challenge, but did not say if he would be playing.

Woods has hosted the Hero World Challenge, an unofficial Tour event, for years now in the Bahamas.

Woods hasn't played anywhere since the crash and has only made a handful of public appearances. It is expected he will compete in the new TGL season in December

If all goes well at the Hero World Challenge physically for Woods, he could then be part of the PNC Championship — an exhibition event that features major champions paired with a family member — from Dec. 17-20 in Orlando where he could play alongside his son, Charlie, and be allowed to use a cart, if needed.

articles.title: Tiger Woods set for competitive golf return in December's Hero World Challenge
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is set to return to competitive golf in December for the first time in more than two years.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is set to return to competitive golf in December for the first time in more than two years.

Woods, 50, has not played in a traditional ranking event since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon amid a series of off-course issues.

The 15-time major champion has endured a challenging few years with a number of injuries and turmoil in his personal life.

Woods will host next month's Hero World Challenge - an event which is part of the PGA Tour schedule but does not carry FedEx Cup points - and has been announced as part of the 20-player field.

The American is one of three exemptions for the tournament in the Bahamas along with compatriots Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland.

Speaking to SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio in a video posted last week, Woods said: "I'm feeling better, no doubt about that.

"I've been training quite a bit. I will be at Hero either way, so I'll see you there."

Woods' long-awaited return comes after he accepted a five-year driving ban in September following a plea agreement in his reckless driving case.

In March, Woods had been arrested and charged with driving under the influence after clipping a truck and rolling his car in Florida.

Woods was also found with two white pills in his pocket, which were identified as hydrocodone - an opioid used to treat pain.

He subsequently stepped away from golf to seek treatment in what was described by his attorney as an "intensive, highly individualised and medically integrated programme".

Woods has endured a succession of debilitating injuries, including multiple back surgeries, serious fractures to his right leg following a car crash in 2021 and a ruptured Achilles tendon in 2025.

Woods also suffered the death of his mother, Kultida, in February 2025, while his girlfriend Vanessa Trump was diagnosed with breast cancer earlier this year.

Trump, the former daughter-in-law of US President Donald Trump, said last month that she is now cancer free.

Analysis: Woods will want to play majors in 2027

Every report we had since Tiger Woods resurfaced into public life has told us he is looking good and looking fit. Going into the new year he will be taking part in his own indoor golf league, the TGL, so it's not the biggest surprise that he will be at his own tournament in the Bahamas.

This is the fifth time he has come back from a long-term absence from the game at this event. It is one that means an awful lot to him. It is involved with his charitable foundation and it's his tournament, so no surprise this is the one he has chosen to come back at.

The TGL in the new year, that's the indoor simulator run by his company in conjunction with Rory McIlroy. He did compete last year and cut a pretty pathetic figure by the standards of someone who has won 15 major titles. We could see him play before that at the PNC event. That's the parent and child event where he would presumably play with his son Charlie.

He is trying to line himself up to play at least the majors next year. They mean an awful lot to him.

We know how much the Masters means to him, but also think about where the US Open is going to be played, at Pebble Beach, and that's where he won the US Open in 2000 by 15 shots.

The Open Championship at St Andrews where he has won two of his three Open titles. These would be events he would certainly want to be at.

articles.summary: El 'León de Barrika' se afianza en el 'top 10' del ranking mundial
articles.body: El último empujón de la temporada ha llevado a Jon Rahm hasta el sexto puesto del ranking mundial (OWGR). Los cinco jugadores que tiene por delante todavía conservan una importante ventaja sobre el ‘León de Barrika’, pero no cabe duda de que este ha aprovechado bien la primera temporada en la que los torneos de LIV Golf puntuaban y su regularidad lo está haciendo 'volar'. Cuando se marchó del PGA era segundo en la lista mundial. El vizcaíno ha ganado este año dos veces (Hong Kong y México) en la ya extinta liga y ha cosechado nueve ‘top 5’ en total. Lejos de LIV, recientemente venció en el Abu Dhabi Championship, fue 19º en el torneo final y en los Majors sólo brilló en el PGA Championship, donde terminó segundo. El siguiente español mejor colocado es Eugenio López-Chacarra, que es ya trigésimo cuarto del mundo y eso que sólo ha podido jugar un grande este año. Ha quedado segundo de la Race to Dubai (clasificación anual del DP World Tour), sólo superado por McIlroy y su escalada ha sido espectacular. Esta temporada se ha anotado tres victorias (KLM Open, Open de Italia e India Championship) y hasta el propio Rory lo ve ya como un jugador Ryder. Eugenio se ha ganado su lugar en el PGA Tour en 2027, pero por el momento Rahm es quien no tiene asegurada su presencia en este circuito el año que viene. El epicentro deportivo del vasco estará en el DP World Tour y el comisionado del PGA, Brian Rolapp, ha dejado claro que de momento no van a resucitar el ‘Programa de Miembros que Regresan’ al que se acogió Brooks Koepka. "Hemos escuchado a nuestros aficionados y sabemos que quieren que los mejores jugadores jueguen juntos, y compartimos esa opinión", dijo Rolapp después de una reunión de la junta directiva donde el PGA Tour aprobó los detalles de su nueva estructura competitiva, que debutará en 2028. "Desde el primer día que asumí el cargo, he dicho que me interesa hacer todo lo posible para mejorar el PGA Tour”, añadió el dirigente, que parece dar a entender que él podría estar dispuesto a negociar algún acuerdo. Eso sí, dejó claro que no depende exclusivamente de una parte: “Dicho esto, como somos una organización de miembros, tenemos reglas y, como ya comenté, existen para garantizar la equidad y el equilibrio competitivo. Las reglas importan y se harán cumplir. Hoy mantuvimos una conversación profunda con ambas directivas [PGA y representantes de los jugadores] sobre la situación de los golfistas salientes del LIV. Por lo que sabemos, el proceso de bancarrota continúa y es complejo. Espero poder ofrecer más información a principios del nuevo año, pero hasta entonces, no especularé sobre el resultado ni sobre las decisiones individuales que tomen los jugadores”.

articles.title: Tiger Woods to make long-awaited golf return at Hero World Challenge
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is set to compete in a golf tournament for the first time in more than two years at the Hero World Challenge. Read more details here:
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is ready to return to professional golf, and he's now set a date for when his comeback officially begins.

After multiple injuries and setbacks, Woods has committed to play in next month's Hero World Challenge with some of the PGA Tour's top players. This will be the first time Woods competes in a professional golf tournament in more than two years.

Woods hosts the annual event in the Bahamas, which is slated for Dec. 3-6. He was added to the event through one of three remaining wild-card spots in the 20-golfer field, according to tournament organizers on Tuesday, Nov. 17 . The 50-year-old has been away from competition since The Open Championship in July 2024.

His comeback attempt ahead of last year's Masters was derailed by a DUI arrest and rehab stint stemming from a car crash in March that led to a plea deal and the suspension of his driver's license .

But the 15-time major winner told SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio recently that he was "feeling better. No doubt about that. I've been training quite a bit."

Woods is also expected to play in TGL's 2027 season as a member of Jupiter Links Golf Club beginning next month. The PNC Championship , slated for Dec. 19-20 in Orlando, Florida, is the PGA Tour's annual father-son event that Tiger Woods and Charlie Woods have also been regulars at in recent years. They did not play in last year's event as Tiger Woods recovered from back surgery. Golfweek previously reported that PNC Championship organizers are holding a spot in the 2026 field in case Woods is healthy enough to compete.

Woods announced in October 2025 that he underwent a disc replacement surgery on his lumbar spine. It was the seventh back surgery of his career, and the second in about a year's time after he underwent microdecompression surgery in September 2024. Woods also needed surgery when he ruptured his Achilles in March 2025 while training and practicing at home.

Before the March 2026 incident that led to his arrest and decision to go to rehab, Woods had been working his way back with an eye toward playing in the Masters in 2026. He played in the TGL Finals on March 24 earlier this year.

The Hero World Challenge is a 20-player, limited-field event with no cut. Scottie Scheffler, Justin Thomas and Cameron Young are among the top golfers scheduled to play. Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland also received special tournament invites along with Woods on Tuesday.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau Boosts DP World Tour For 2027 Season
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau joins the DP World Tour with Category One status, bringing massive attention and a pragmatic shift to the 2027 season.
articles.body:
The 2027 DP World Tour season will feature Bryson DeChambeau, The decision changed the competitive landscape after LIV Golf fell apart.. The two-time major champion submitted his application just hours before the November 15 deadline, securing a spot that guarantees entry to every event on the circuit. The application that grants him entry to every circuit event arrives as the American faces a PGA Tour suspension, prompting him to seek a new venue to preserve his competitive standing.

The American's status as a recent major champion earned him 'category one' membership, the highest priority bracket available. This classification ensures he plays any tournament he chooses without needing to qualify through lower-tier events. AOL.com sources indicate that Jon Rahm and DeChambeau, both LIV golfers, cannot play on the PGA Tour next season without special return approval. The situation leaves DeChambeau with a clear path back to the established tours via the DP World Tour, bypassing the immediate restrictions of the American circuit. Sky Sports noted that membership categories for the 2027 season were announced on Tuesday, placing DeChambeau alongside other high-profile players seeking a route back to the mainstream.

DeChambeau's move is not isolated; it is part of a broader realignment of players following the bankruptcy of LIV Golf. Per Sky Sports, Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith, and Bubba Watson, all former major champions, agreed to receive invitations to a set number of tournaments next season. These contracts exclude Rolex Series tournaments but include designated events where players would "add value" to the field. The DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings addressed the shifting dynamics, noting the unique circumstances facing the sport.

"There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months," said DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings. He emphasized that the tour adopted a pragmatic approach to handle this unprecedented situation while keeping the best interests of the entire membership in mind. This strategy allows the tour to integrate former breakaway players without disrupting the core structure of the season. In December, DeChambeau will play in South Africa at Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge, which he confirmed.

The addition of DeChambeau brings a massive digital footprint to the tour. YouTube and Instagram are among the platforms where the Californian counts over 10 million followers and subscribers. "That's an incredibly viable option, I'll tell you that," DeChambeau said earlier this year. However, his recent return to the mainstream suggests a preference for competitive play over pure content creation. This shift was welcomed by Rory McIlroy, who acknowledged the marketing value DeChambeau brings to the sport.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," said McIlroy. The American also addressed his past conduct, including a controversial incident at The Open in July where he argued with officials over a two-shot penalty. He released a statement acknowledging the criticism and citing the philosophy of Arnold Palmer. "Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," DeChambeau said. This admission helped clear the path for his reinstatement into the professional fold.

The integration of these players sets the stage for a highly competitive year. DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings expressed confidence in the upcoming schedule, stating, "Our 2027 season is set to be one of the most keenly contested campaigns in our 55-year history." The presence of multiple former LIV players, including DeChambeau, Rahm, and Smith, ensures that the fields will feature deep talent pools. The tour's ability to accommodate these athletes while maintaining its integrity shows a willingness to adapt to the current realities of professional golf.

DeChambeau's confirmed appearance at the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa this December is the first concrete event for fans to watch him compete under his new DP World Tour membership.

articles.title: DeChambeau Joins DP World Tour For 2027 After PGA Suspension
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau joins the DP World Tour for 2027 while facing a one-year PGA Tour ban. See the full list of returning LIV stars and what this means for the...
articles.body:
For the 2027 season, Bryson DeChambeau has signed up with the DP World Tour. He must sit out the American circuit for a full year as punishment for his time with LIV Golf. This move comes just after the two-time major champion applied for membership hours before the Sunday deadline. The news was confirmed by James Corrigan of The Telegraph and reported by Golf Business News on Tuesday.

DeChambeau will compete as a Category 1 member. This status grants him automatic entry to every event on the tour. He joins a group of 22 major champions who hold exempt status for next year. Next month in South Africa, the American will begin his new chapter at the Nedbank Golf Challenge before the season fully opens.

The DP World Tour took a practical approach to welcome back former LIV players. Guy Kinnings, the tour's Chief Executive, noted that the golf world has changed a lot in the last 12 months. He stated that the tour must act with the best interests of all members in mind. The goal is to add value to tournaments without hurting current players.

Nine former LIV golfers signed agreements for specific event invitations. Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith, and Bubba Watson are among those returning. These deals do not include the high-stakes Rolex Series events. The tour wants to keep the fields strong while protecting the rights of existing members. This balance is key to making the 2027 season work for everyone.

DeChambeau had other options but chose the competitive route. He could have focused on his YouTube channel and only played majors. He has more than 10 million followers on platforms like YouTube and Instagram. Earlier this year, he admitted that going that route was "an incredibly viable option, I'll tell you that," DeChambeau said.

Instead, he decided to return to the mainstream. He promised to move forward with respect for the game and its history.

The 2027 season will feature 199 players from 29 different countries. This number includes players who qualified through various global pathways. The tour announced these membership categories on Sunday after the 2026 Race to Dubai ended. The field looks deeper than it did a year ago.

Many top names have already signed up for the European circuit. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, and Sergio Garcia are all returning. Almost every prominent former LIV player has rejoined the tour. This creates a very competitive field for the upcoming year.

DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings called the upcoming year historic. "Our 2027 season is set to be one of the most keenly contested campaigns in our 55-year history," Kinnings said. The tour has seen three of its members win major championships in 2026. These wins showed that their players can compete on the global stage.

DeChambeau joins a long list of exempt major champions. The full list includes Rory McIlroy, Justin Thomas, and Jon Rahm. It also features veterans like Graeme McDowell, Lee Westwood, and Henrik Stenson. The mix of old stars and new talent should make for exciting golf.

The PGA Tour has made it clear that DeChambeau cannot play in the US yet. The American circuit will enforce a one-year ban on players who stayed with LIV until its collapse. This rule applies to DeChambeau and Jon Rahm. They must wait until August 2027 to return to the US circuit.

This program helped some players return last year. The lack of a return path forces stars like DeChambeau to look overseas. The DP World Tour is now the only place for them to play regularly.

DeChambeau had a rocky relationship with the game recently. He argued with officials over a two-shot penalty at the Open in July. That behavior disappointed many fans. His decision to join the DP World Tour signals a change in attitude. He wants to grow the game rather than fight against it.

"Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me. My passion has been to grow this game," DeChambeau said. This statement marks a clear break from his previous conduct. The tour accepts this new approach and welcomes him back.

The BMW Australian PGA Championship will launch the 2027 DP World Tour season at the end of November. DeChambeau is not currently in the field for that specific event. He will likely start his season in January at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic. That $9 million tournament will feature many of the returning stars.

articles.title: Luther Burden injury update is exactly what Bears needed after bye week
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears got a promising injury update on WR Luther Burden III.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are off to a great start and are in an epic NFC North battle for first place. They're 7-2 but have the same record as the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings .

Their franchise quarterback, Caleb Williams , has been awesome and has avoided a serious hamstring injury. Williams has thrown for over 1500 yards with eight touchdown passes. He has also added two rushing touchdowns.

The Bears offense has been excellent this season, and they've scored at least 27 points in their four-game winning streak. One key member of their offense is Luther Burden III , and Chicago got a promising injury update on their wide receiver.

What's the latest injury update on Luther Burden III?

Chicago Bears and their fans can breathe a sigh of relief as head coach Ben Johnson says wide receiver Luther Burden III has cleared concussion protocol.

Burden left late in their Week 9 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with a concussion. The Bears secured a 27-24 win in that contest. Burden was solid in that matchup with 97 receiving yards and one touchdown.

Chicago will be happy to have the electrifying wideout back in the lineup. He can take the top off a defense but also burn you with speed. The Missouri product leads the team in receiving yards with 644 and has found the end zone four times this season.

Should you start Burden III in your fantasy football matchup? It is a tad risky because of the concussion, and you never really know how a player is going to react after an injury like that.

If you're in bye-week hell or desperate, tossing #10 in your lineup wouldn't be a bad choice. The Bears' Week 11 matchup is with the New Orleans Saints .

articles.title: Dan Hicks cause of death revealed: How did NBC Sports broadcaster die?
articles.summary: A new report shed more light on the cause of death for NBC Sports broadcaster Dan Hicks after his unexpected passing.
articles.body:
Longtime NBC Sports broadcaster Dan Hicks died from a type of pneumonia, according to a new report.

Hicks passed away at 5:32 p.m. ET on Nov. 11 in a Greenwich, Connecticut hospital, and a copy of his death certificate listed an immediate cause of death as multifocal pneumonia, the California Post reported . Hicks was 64 years old.

Hicks' wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, announced his death the next morning and stated her husband died of an "acute illness." Multifocal pneumonia is an infection that affects multiple areas of the lungs rather than being confined to a single spot.

Golfers who have won PGA Tour events in 2026 season

Hicks had also been dealing with a pulmonary edema (fluid buildup in the lungs) that was preceded by an upper respiratory infection and autoimmune hemolytic anemia, according to the report.

The tributes for Hicks have come from every part of the sports and sports broadcasting world since his sudden passing became public. He spent 35 years with NBC, recently covering the PGA Tour and calling Notre Dame football. He was scheduled to handle play-by-play duties for last weekend's game in South Bend, Indiana, in the "Holy War" battle between the Fighting Irish and Boston College alongside analyst Jason Garrett and sideline reporter Caroline Pineda.

Hicks called iconic moments as a play-by-play announcer in golf, college football and the Olympics, including the 2008 Summer Games in Beijing, when the U.S. men's 4x100-meter freestyle relay swimming team, led by Michael Phelps, made one of the greatest comebacks in Olympic history to set a world record and take home the gold medal.

"Dan was truly one of a kind and quite simply the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter, and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful, and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered," Storm said on social media. "Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time."
