articles.title: Govt reviews Adani project; company says cost remains 5,675 crore
articles.summary: MUMBAI: State forest minister Ganesh Naik chaired a meeting on Tuesday to review Adani Green Energy Ltd's (AGEL) proposed 1,500 MW pumped storage
articles.body: MUMBAI: State forest minister Ganesh Naik chaired a meeting on Tuesday to review Adani Green Energy Ltd's (AGEL) proposed 1,500 MW pumped storage hydroelectric project at Tarali in Patan taluka of Satara district, which ran into a controversy following the company's projection of a lower environmental cost on the adjoining region which is ecologically sensitive.According to official sources, the govt may consider withdrawing the forest department's demand seeking 4% of the total project cost towards wildlife conservation around the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve and Koyna Wildlife Sanctuary.The 4% demand was made on AGEL by way of a letter issued by Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife).The company has clarified that the total estimated capital cost of the project is Rs 5,675 crore, while the Rs 56.75 crore cited earlier as project cost referred only to the phase dealing with survey, investigation, geological exploration, engineering studies, detailed design, field investigations, testing and other preliminary activities for feasibility assessment. It said wildlife clearance was sought for these preliminary works. The proposal was cleared by the State Board for Wildlife in March, and 1% of the applicable cost related to the survey and investigation proposal was deposited with the govt.Tuesday's meeting, attended by AGEL officials, reviewed project requirements, environmental conservation measures and recommendations from the forest department, with focus on balancing infrastructure development and ecosystem protection.Officials also discussed the eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around the wildlife sanctuary. With no specific ESZ notification in place, a 10-km radius applies on the project as per Supreme Court guidelines.In a written clarification to the chief wildlife warden and the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife), AGEL said the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) granted environmental clearance in Feb last year and the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board granted "consent to establish" in April. The company stated no forest land is involved, and a non-forest land NOC has already been obtained.After completing formalities and obtaining a go-ahead from the State Board for Wildlife for site investigations, the company said it submitted a fresh proposal on Nov 5 seeking National Board for Wildlife approval for the full project, with the project cost stated as Rs 5,675 crore, matching the cost mentioned in the environmental clearance.The state forest department issued a stop-work notice on Nov 13 directing work at the project site to be halted, citing commencement of work without National Board for Wildlife approval.AGEL's clarification comes after Satara's Honorary Wildlife Warden, Rohan Bhate, last month flagged an alleged discrepancy in the project cost declared to the state govt, stating it was shown as ₹56.75 crore instead of ₹5,675 crore.In representations to the NBWL, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), and the chief minister, he sought an independent inquiry, arguing that an understated cost could amount to misrepresentation and could affect wildlife conservation contributions linked to project value.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Digboi Golf: Despite leg injury, Rathi takes two-shot lead after first round
articles.summary: DIGBOI: Away from Delhi-NCR’s hazardous air quality, Gurugram golfer Saurav Rathi topped the leaderboard with a seven-under 65 in the first round at
articles.body: DIGBOI: Away from Delhi-NCR’s hazardous air quality, Gurugram golfer Saurav Rathi topped the leaderboard with a seven-under 65 in the first round at Digboi Golf Links here on Tuesday.Playing with an injured leg, the 24-year-old made eight birdies and dropped his only shot of the day on the closing hole, a par-4 18th, to take a two-shot lead on an opening day when only 29 players from a field of 120 managed to break par. It was an impressive start to the 2026-27 PGTI season for Rathi at Assam’s iconic golf course.“It was a solid round and a good start to the new season. I was five-under after nine holes, made two more birdies on the 11th and 12th, followed by another birdie on the 14th. I made pars after that before dropping a disappointing bogey on the 18th from the middle of the fairway, just 40 yards out,” Rathi said after the round.Rathi was joined near the top by 21-year-old Anshul Kabthiyal and Players’ Championship 2026 winner Om Prakash Chouhan, who shared second place at five-under 67.Rathi, a regular on PGTI since 2019, recently secured his full playing rights for the new season after finishing 17th at PGTI Qualifying Tournament Final Stage in Ahmedabad. Despite nursing a leg injury sustained after slipping on wet stairs at the golf course on Monday, Rathi produced a commanding display, hitting 12 of 14 fairways and 15 greens in regulation.“I think the injury has actually helped me because I normally play a little fast. Since I’m not able to walk properly, I’ve had to slow myself down, and I think that’s helping my game,” he said, adding that he hoped to “strike the ball the same way I did today and make some putts”.Playing for the sixth time in India's longest-running golf tournament, Rathi also didn't shy away from expressing his appreciation of the weather here.“It’s a great course! I’m from Delhi and it's worth coming all the way here just because of the weather. The amenities here also very good, so I always like playing here.”Meanwhile, Kabthiyal’s opening 67 featured an eagle on the par-5 seventh, five birdies and two bogeys.The experienced Chouhan, an 11-time PGTI winner, former European Challenge Tour winner and the 2023 PGTI rankings champion, also carded a 67, making eight birdies against three bogeys.Four players shared fourth place at four-under 68, including Gurugram’s Kushal Singh, Pune’s Divyansh Dubey, Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh and Lucknow’s Sanjeev Kumar.Kushal made seven birdies and three bogeys, while Divyansh registered six birdies and two bogeys. Yuvraj recovered from a double-bogey on the par-5 15th and another bogey with seven birdies, while Sanjeev produced five birdies against a lone bogey.Despite measuring just 6,348 yards, the par-72 course presented a stern opening-round test, with only 29 players in the field returning sub-par scores.(The writer is in Digboi on an invitation from DP World PGTI)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour: Which other ex-LIV Golf players feature and what does it mean for men's golf?
articles.summary: Over 30 ex-LIV Golf players will feature on the DP World Tour next season, with Bryson DeChambeau set to feature full-time after accepting membership; What impact will it have on past members and why have some earning cards divided opinion?
articles.body:
Membership categories for the 2027 DP World Tour season were announced on Tuesday, with DeChambeau applying before the November 15 deadline and taking category one status - the highest priority ranking - for his 2024 US Open victory.

DeChambeau's future was uncertain after LIV Golf's collapse earlier this month, with him ineligible on the PGA Tour next season, but the two-time major champion is one of over 30 players from the breakaway circuit now set to feature on the DP World Tour.

Many already had DP World Tour status, including nine taking category 11 membership via the career money list, while nine - including Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith - signed agreements to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments in 2027.

"I think he [DeChambeau] is going to be a great addition, he's going to bring interest and I think it's good, but I think he's very fortunate and I think all the LIV Golf players are incredibly fortunate," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports News .

"They [LIV players] basically are not skipping a beat here. They're coming back into the fold again having worked for LIV, that worked very strongly against the DP World Tour in terms of stealing away a lot of the business.

"They are very fortunate that they are getting an opportunity to play in the DP World next year, which is an excellent tour, with excellent prize funds, and obviously an opportunity to play the following year on the PGA Tour with all the riches over there."

What impact will invites have on previous members?

Abraham Ancer, Lucas Herbert, Michael La Sasso, Joaquin Niemann, Carlos Ortiz and Thomas Pieters have joined major winners Johnson, Smith, Bubba Watson in signing an invites-based agreement, which will exclude Rolex Series events.

The DP World Tour admit the decision will bring 'different viewpoints' but insist it will not reduce playing opportunities for existing members, with invites designed to 'add value to tournaments'.

"The players to have accepted this invite rule, they're going to be sent to these places like the Magical Kenya or the China Classic or whatever it might be," Sky Sports' Tim Barter explained on the Sky Sports Golf podcast.

"Those tournaments sometimes didn't have anyone in the top 50 in the world in them, occasionally only one player in the top hundred in the world, so they are going to really to bring some star power.

"I think Guy Kinnings took it very seriously when players started to say to him, maybe that the rank-and-file players on the DP World Tour, 'we shouldn't be missing out on opportunities to play because these guys are being invited'.

"What he's doing is obviously putting them [invites to ex-LIV Golf members] into events where it goes through most of the categories. Nobody who won a card at tour school or the HotelPlanner Tour or the main tour will actually miss out, it looks like."

Which ex-LIV Golf players will play on the DP World Tour?

Winners of major championships since 2022 earn category one membership, with Jon Rahm joining DeChambeau in that list, while Tyrrell Hatton - winner of the DP World Tour Championship on Sunday - in category two.

Laurie Canter and Adrian Meronk hold category three membership for a victory in the previous two seasons and David Puig is in the category below, with priority access given to the lowest numbers when finalising a tournament field.

Thomas Detry , Tom McKibbin and Victor Perez are Category 10 members, while Ryder Cup legends Sergio Garcia , Lee Westwood , Paul Casey , Graeme McDowell and Martin Kaymer all qualify via the Career Money List.

Branden Grace, Charl Schwartzel , Ian Poulter and Louis Oosthuizen also hold DP World Tour membership via the money list, albeit in a slightly lower category, although any who previously resigned from the circuit are understood to face a 10-tournament suspension before being eligible to return to action.

Josele Ballester , Byeong Hun An and John Catlin progressed through Qualifying School to claim category 18 status, while those agreeing a specific number of invites can secure DP World Tour membership with a victory. Others ex-LIV members may secure spots in events co-sanctioned with different tours.

Could previous DP World Tour members 'lose out'?

It remains unclear how many PGA Tour cards will be available via the Race to Dubai after next season, with a significant reduction from the 10 currently on offer expected, leaving it tougher to progress from the DP World Tour.

Those further down the rankings may find it harder to keep their DP World Tour membership, with LIV Golf additions adding additional depth to a circuit where only the top 100 at the end of the campaign retain full playing privileges.

"We've seen two ex-LIV players winning in the last two weeks and we're likely to see a lot of ex-LIV players winning in the coming months on the DP World Tour," McGinley added.

"They [ex-LIV golfers] are probably going to take 20 or 30 of the 100 DP World Tour cards that are available, so there's really 20 or 30 less spots for the current players to play for next year in terms of keeping their status.

"That's to be a difficult scenario for them and they didn't get the riches that the guys went to LIV did, so I can understand why they're feeling aggrieved.

"I'm just hoping that the DP World Tour players, who have remained loyal, come out next year and play well with all these LIV players in the field. Somebody is going to lose out in the years to come and that's what's the unfortunate about this whole sorry mess."

Why the DP World Tour could be 'stronger than ever'

The earliest LIV Golf players would currently be able to feature on the PGA Tour is the FedExCup Fall in the autumn, depending on their based membership status, leaving DP World Tour events with stronger fields during the bulk of the 2027 season.

DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings said the forthcoming season could 'be one of the most keenly contested campaign' in their history, following a 'significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf'.

"There's going to be lots of eyes on the DP World Tour, Sky Sports' Andrew Coltart admitted. "There's some huge names playing a full season and maybe more than four of them will be coming back for the next year.

"Obviously it [LIV players featuring] is going to put the nose out of joint for some members. This is specifically designed to enhance the strength of tournaments and not have a massive impact on them.

"The DP World Tour is going to be as strong as it's ever been next year and certainly very strong in 2028."

articles.title: Northeast has huge potential, but it’s still largely untapped: PGTI CEO Amandeep Johl
articles.summary: DIGBOI: Living just 250 yards from the first tee of a golf course, Amandeep Johl took up the sport at the age of seven.
articles.body: DIGBOI: Living just 250 yards from the first tee of a golf course, Amandeep Johl took up the sport at the age of seven. Since then, golf has remained an integral part of his life. In 2004, he co-founded the Asian Tour and contributed to the early institutional framework of professional golf in the region. Now serving as CEO of the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI), Johl spoke to TOI on the sidelines of the 26th Masters Golf Tournament here.Excerpts:What is the importance of a tournament like the Masters?It has grown from a small tournament and has now become a Rs 1 crore prize money event. So, it’s a very important tournament, firstly because of the prize money and secondly because it’s one of the few such tournaments in Assam and the Northeast.We are trying to promote Assam as a golf destination in India. I think Indian Oil has been a great supporter of sports, and golf in particular, as a public sector company. There is also the Petroleum Sports Control Board Golf Tournament, which has been held for many years. A lot of golfers owe their success to Indian Oil. We have golfers who have played for and secured jobs with Indian Oil.So, this tournament holds a very strategic position in the growth of golf in India because Indian Oil supports players and provides them with a livelihood through jobs and scholarships. It also organises tournaments where, once a player turns professional, they can earn prize money.How has the golf landscape in the country changed since your days as a player, coach and now CEO of PGTI?I think there has been a sea change since we got Kapil Dev as the president of PGTI. Since he is a legendary cricketer who is now supporting golf, it has made a huge difference. It sends out a strong message when legends from one sport cross over to support others. He sees huge potential in this game because it is not a team sport but an individual one. There is no team selection. There is nothing that can stop someone if he or she is playing well.I feel golf in India has grown by leaps and bounds over the last two or three years. We have seen almost a 50% growth in both the number of tournaments and their prize money. With DP World joining as title sponsor, several brands such as HCL, Amul, Axis Bank, Amrutanjan, Air India, Indian Oil and Trident have also become associated with the sport. So, we feel the sky's the limit for Indian golf.What do you feel about the prospects of golf in the Northeast?The Northeast has huge potential, but it remains largely untapped, in my opinion. For example, a state like Assam can probably have four or five international-level golf courses. But there isn’t even one of that standard at the moment. We are trying to reach out to the state government because sport is a state subject. We are trying to reach out to Himanta Biswa Sarma to find out if the government can provide us with land.Golf courses can be investment magnets as well as tourism magnets. I believe India needs 300 golf courses. Even if we start building 10 every year over the next decade, we will still barely reach our potential.What do you say to people who believe golf is an elite or rich man’s sport?I don’t think it is. But even if it is, five-star hotels are also for the rich. Does the state not support them? Does an airline not have a business class? So why are we so against golf, even if it is considered an elite sport? We are trying to work towards Viksit Bharat, which aims to make India a developed nation with a per capita income of over $25,000. If that is what we are working towards, why should we be against golf? I’m not disputing that it is an elite sport, but it is also an aspirational sport.How important is golf’s return to the Olympics?It’s very important. I think Indian girls are doing much better than the boys. We have seen players like Pranavi and Diksha Dagar perform consistently at the international level. Diksha, one of my students, has won two gold medals at the Deaflympics. She also plays regularly on the Ladies European Tour and was part of the Indian team that won silver at the Asian Games. So, I feel the girls are doing very well. But it is only a matter of time before the boys start performing too.(The writer is in Digboi on an invitation from DP World PGTI)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Arin Ahuja rides waves of golf, dreams of making it big on global stage
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For 22-years-old Arin Ahuja, golf was never part of a carefully drawn career plan.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For 22-years-old Arin Ahuja, golf was never part of a carefully drawn career plan. It began with a simple family routine in 2011, when his father, who was associated with the US Golf Club in Mumbai started taking him and his brother along to the course. What started as a way to spend an afternoon soon developed into a passion, eventually setting him on the path towards professional golf.At just seven years old, Arin, who is from Noida, found himself fascinated by the game. Initially, it was all about hitting a few balls, playing around with the golf carts and challenging the caddies to put on contests. However, those casual visits gradually turned into something much bigger. Fifteen years later, the young golfer is beginning to make his mark, having topped the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) Qualifying School and taken a significant step towards establishing himself on the professional circuit.The transition from amateur golf to the professional circuit, however, has brought an entirely different set of challenges. Having spent the last few years competing in amateur tournaments, Arin is now learning what it takes to consistently compete against some of the country's established professionals."Once you make that shift, you need to be more deliberate about everything. You need to know yourself well, understand your statistics and record everything you do on the course so that you can improve. Playing 12 or 13 events a year on the national circuit also gives you more exposure. You learn how to analyse different situations, react to them and then work on those aspects after the tournament," he said.Arin draws inspiration from two of golf's biggest names, Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy. While both have influenced his approach to the sport, it is Woods' competitive mentality that particularly resonates with him."He just had that attitude where he needed to do it. He never backed down, no matter what. He wanted to win and was aggressive about everything. He was intimidating for other players as well. That inspired me to be a bit like him on the golf course," Arin said.However, the youngster is equally conscious of developing his own identity. Rather than getting distracted by what others are doing, he prefers to remain focused on his game and maintain control over his emotions.Golf, after all, is a sport of fine margins, where a disappointing round can quickly test a player's patience. Arin believes one of the most important lessons he has learnt is to accept setbacks rather than fight them. With tournaments regularly lined up on the calendar, he knows there is always another opportunity to put things right."If you have a bad tournament, I feel you should let the emotions sink in for a day or two. I am fortunate to have a good team behind me in the form of my parents and coach. We sit down, discuss what went wrong and what went right, and then go back to the drawing board to correct the mistakes," he explained.His triumph at the PGTI Qualifying School has provided further encouragement. For a young golfer making his way into the professional ranks, topping the qualifying event is an important confidence booster and an indication that the work being put in is beginning to deliver results.Arin is also optimistic about the growing opportunities within Indian professional golf. He believes the increasing prize money and competitiveness on the PGTI circuit have made the sport a more attractive career option for aspiring professionals."The PGTI has helped not just me but all the professionals on tour. The prize money has gone up, the competition has become tighter and there are so many more avenues open to players now. When you put in 7-8 hours every day at the golf course, winning an event like this is good validation that your hard work is paying off," he said.He believes that golfers who consistently perform among the top 40 on the domestic circuit can build a sustainable professional career, provided they continue to put in the necessary work.Beyond the technical aspects, Arin has also been working on developing a stronger mental approach. Since beginning his association with coach Raul, he feels certain technical adjustments have helped him find greater consistency."You understand over a period of time that golf is not always going to be up. It has its ups and downs, so you learn to accept that and not fight it too much. You just ride the waves. If things are going down, you know they will eventually go up again," he said.He also credits Indian golfer Shubhankar Sharma for offering valuable advice during a difficult phase. Following a disappointing tournament, a conversation with Sharma reinforced the importance of self-belief."He told me that you have to ride the waves in this game and trust yourself. Self-belief is the most important thing in golf. It takes you wherever you want to go," Arin recalled.But behind the youngster's progress is a support system that has remained his biggest strength. His father, who served in the Army, and his brother, who is also in the armed forces, have instilled in him a sense of discipline and perseverance. His mother, too, has been a constant source of encouragement."There have been moments when I felt like leaving the game because I wasn't playing well. But my family pushed me to keep going. My father and brother have that mindset that you always have to keep at it. Things are not easy, but you still have to persevere. It is because of them that I am here today," he said.For now, the ambition is to strengthen every aspect of his game, lower his scoring average and gradually earn opportunities to compete internationally. The ultimate dream is to make it to the PGA Tour, but Arin knows that the journey will require patience and consistent performances.Having already taken an important step with his Q-School triumph, Arin is beginning to turn childhood curiosity into professional ambition. And if there is one lesson he has carried from his journey so far, it is that success in golf is as much about believing in yourself through the difficult days as it is about celebrating the good ones.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: John Daly still gambles despite losing $1.65M in one night after Tiger Woods playoff loss
articles.summary: John Daly lost $1.65 million in Las Vegas after his 2005 playoff loss to Tiger Woods, but the two-time major champion admits he still gambles as an escape.
articles.body: Golf legend John Daly said he still enjoys gambling despite losing $1.65 million in Las Vegas following a playoff loss to Tiger Woods and explained why he continues to play slot machines years later. "I told my caddie and everybody ... 'Look, man, I should have won that damn tournament. I don't want this money,'" Daly recalled on Sean Hannity's "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast. "I'm going to go to Wynn and play the $5,000 slot machine. And if I win, I win. If I don't, I don't." FANDUEL, BRYCE HARPER VIDEO TO LOSING GAMBLER REINFORCES THE GREED OF THE MLB, SPORTSBOOKS AND THE UNION The two-time major champion was reflecting on his 2005 playoff loss to Tiger Woods at the WGC-American Express Championship, where he earned $750,000 for finishing second. He then headed to Las Vegas, where he said he lost $1.65 million gambling — more than double his tournament winnings. "If you're pulling $5,000 a pull, it don't take long," Daly explained. Despite the $1.65 million loss, Daly said he still gambles, but he now approaches it differently. "Now I go in there, stare at a slot machine, going like, 'I am getting away from the world right now,'" he explained, adding that he now bets less per spin. DR MARC SIEGEL: THE ANGELS BEHIND ALCOHOLICS ANONYMOUS STILL INSPIRE HOPE "I'm not the blackjack guy anymore. I go in to just get away from the world, you know? It's a little escape for me." Daly also discussed his struggles with alcohol, the highs and lows of his career, his Christian faith and his relationship with President Donald Trump. "I love him as a human being, as a father, as a family guy and most powerful man in the world trying to protect America," he said when asked about playing golf with the president. "He's already got his life set and money. He doesn't care about money," Daly added as the conversation turned to politics. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Without naming a political party, Daly appeared to criticize Democrats following their sweeping 2026 midterm election victories, questioning why voters supported candidates he said had "no policies." "Let's take the other side of that ... all they care about is filling their pockets, and that just really pisses me off. They're going to spend two years trying to impeach him, Pete [Hegseth], trying to impeach everybody, and what I don't understand is the people voted for these people with no policies," he said. Viewers can watch or listen to Hannity's full conversation with Daly on the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast, available on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and iHeartRadio.

articles.title: CME Group Tour Championship: Field, format, prize money as Nelly Korda, Charley Hull, Lottie Woad battle for win at LPGA finale
articles.summary: Key questions about the CME Group Tour Championship, as the LPGA Tour’s 2026 season-long points race comes to an end; watch all four rounds live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
What is the CME Group Tour Championship?

The CME Group Tour Championship is the final event in the LPGA Tour's season-long points race.

Throughout 2026, players have competed in the LPGA Tour's points competition, the Race to CME Globe.

The top 60 players on the Race to CME Globe Points List are invited to feature at this weekend's event and the player who wins the 2026 CME Group Tour Championship will be crowned the Race to CME Globe champion.

Where is the CME Group Tour Championship held?

The tournament is held at the Tiburon Golf Club at the Ritz-Carlton Golf Resort in Naples, Florida.

The course has hosted the tournament since 2013.

It is the second time in consecutive years that Korda has arrived at the CME Group Tour Championship sitting at the top of the Race to CME Globe standings.

The American has already been crowned the Rolex Player of the Year, with three events to spare, but has never won the Race to CME Group Tour Championship. A first title this week would see her qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

Standing in her way is a field of the LPGA Tour's best players, including two-time CME Group Tour Championship winner Jeeno Thitikul , who arrives in Florida having won four times on the LPGA Tour this season.

Miyu Yamashita , who has three wins on the LPGA Tour in 2026, enjoyed a strong finish to her season, winning twice while placing inside the top 10 three times in her last six events.

Haeran Ryu , who clinched back-to-back majors at The Amundi Evian Championship and the KPMG Women's PGA Championship, also comes into this event off the back of a fine vein of form, finishing tied-second and tied-third in her last two starts.

Hull clinched the first LPGA Tour title of her career at this event back in 2016, so she certainly knows how to win at Tiburon Golf Club.

It's been a great year for Hull, who won the Solheim Cup with Team Europe in September and placed inside the top 10 at five LPGA Tour events. She'll no doubt want to end the season in style with a win.

Woad is the only other English player in the field. She too has enjoyed an excellent year, winning the Kroger Queen City Championship in May and finishing tied-ninth at last week's The ANNIKA, marking her seventh top-10 finish of the season.

A total prize purse of £8.33m ($11m) is up for grabs, with the winner set to take home a £3.03m ($4m) cheque, the biggest cash prize in the history of women's golf.

The runner-up is also set to receive £757,423 ($1m).

What other end-of-season awards are up for grabs?

The LPGA Tour will also award the golfer with the lowest scoring average across the 2026 season with The Vare Trophy.

While Korda holds the lowest average score for the year, she has not played enough rounds to qualify for the award, meaning Yamashita, who has a scoring average of 69.50 and Thitikul, who follows her at 69.87, will battle it out to win The Vare Trophy.

How to watch the CME Group Tour Championship?

Sky Sports will be showing all four rounds of the CME Group Tour Championship live.

The first two rounds of the tournament will be shown live on Sky Sports Mix from 7pm on Thursday and Friday, with the action also live from 8pm on both days.

The third round coverage starts at 6pm on Saturday on both Sky Sports Mix and Sky Sports Golf, while Sunday's action is also live from 6pm on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports+ .

Coverage of the final round will begin at 6pm on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Kai Trump makes declaration about ‘next step’ after college golf
articles.summary: Kai Trump, the granddaughter of United States President Donald Trump, is gearing up to start golfing for the Univeristy of Miami, and is ready to do away wit...
articles.body:
Kai Trump, the granddaughter of United States President Donald Trump, is gearing up to start golfing for the Univeristy of Miami, and is ready to do away with any preconceived notions about her that may stem from who her grandfather is.

"Because of my family and stuff like that," she says of why people think they already know what she's about, per Women's Golf Magazine. "But I love how there are people who may not be fans of my family but love me and love watching my golf content."

Surprisingly, Kai isn't interested in going into the family business of politics, and wants to get to the top of the golf world.

"I'm excited to start college golf," Trump says. "I'm also looking forward to being part of a team, having the team culture in college, and honestly, just getting my game better, preparing for the next level."

Surprisingly, for Kai, the next level is the LPGA.

"I want to go pro eventually," she says. "So, by doing that, I feel like college golf will get me ready for the next level."

The young Miami Hurricanes golfer said that growing up in such a famous family has helped her develop the thick skin she needs to excel at her sport.

"You have to learn to have thick skin on the golf course," she said. "Sometimes it will go your way and sometimes it won't."

"You might not play well some days or weeks, but you have to move on and stick with the process," she added.

For now, her focus is on her career at Miami and being able to respond to the difficulties that are bound to come with collegiate golfing.

"I've worked really hard to get where I am today," Trump says. "It's definitely a long road, but if you want something, you'll do everything in your power to get it."

articles.title: Brooks Koepka: American labels his 2026 PGA Tour season a 'disappointment' and targets 2027 Ryder Cup spot
articles.summary: Brooks Koepka will tee up in the RSM Classic this weekend; the American left LIV Golf in 2025 and returned to the PGA Tour earlier this year but has endured a tough season; watch the RSM Classic live on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
The American returned to the PGA Tour via the one-time-only Returning Member Program in January following his LIV Golf exit at the end of 2025, a decision he said he was "beyond happy with".

After being welcomed back to the tour with open arms, Koepka made his return at the Farmers Insurance Open in February. He'd go on to make 16 starts on the PGA Tour this year but would miss the cut at five events and record only one top-10 finish.

Koepka, who was not selected as one of Keegan Bradley's captain's picks for the 2025 Ryder Cup and was also omitted from Brandt Snedeker's President's Cup team in 2026, hopes to raise his game and earn a spot in the roster for next year's Ryder Cup.

"Adare Manor is a big goal of mine," Koepka said. "But this year has just been a little bit of a disappointment, so I know I need to pick it up a little bit.

"It's something I don't enjoy, sitting back watching the Presidents Cup.

"I know I've only played in one [2017], a lot of those [omissions are due to] injuries. But those team events are a lot of fun, I really enjoy them.

"Getting to be around the guys and representing your country is pretty cool.

"So, anytime you can do that, or you have the opportunity to, and you're not able to go play, it kind of infuriates me sitting on the sidelines."

The 36-year-old has featured in four Ryder Cup's in the past, notably helping Team USA to victory in at Hazletine in 2016 and Whistling Straits in 2020.

He boasts an overall individual record of 7-6-2.

'The reception was fantastic from the players'

Koepka was the lone player to elect to sign up to the PGA Tour's Returning Member Program, with Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith all snubbing the deal , instead choosing to remain at LIV Golf in 2026.

However, following the dissolution of the formerly Saudi-backed breakaway league, Rahm, DeChambeau and Smith have all elected to rejoin the DP World Tour for the 2027 season, along with multiple other former LIV Golf players.

Koepka, meanwhile, was asked ahead of this week's RSM Classic whether he felt back at home after returning to the PGA Tour, replying: "Yeah, I felt very at peace with coming back.

"The reception was fantastic from all the players, caddies, just everybody on tour.

"I think I kept a good relationship with everybody even when I left.

"I think that played probably a huge part in that.

"Everybody was really receptive. I loved the conversations that I've had just throughout the year, just guys asking what was going on, thought process and how things went and the decisions made to get back here.

"Everything was great. I'm beyond happy with my decision."

articles.title: Pelicans Get Bad News on Potential Dejounte Murray Trade Partner
articles.summary: Dejounte Murray's trade request faces a new complication as an NBA insider reveals Phoenix's surprising stance. The post Pelicans Get Bad News on Potential D...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans have a willing trade candidate in Dejounte Murray. Finding a team prepared to give them an acceptable return could prove more difficult.

One potential destination appears less promising than initially believed.

The Phoenix Suns aren't actively shopping Jalen Green or searching for a point guard, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer , casting doubt on a possible deal involving Murray.

Speaking Tuesday on Bleacher Report's "NBA Insider Notebook," Fischer pushed back on reports suggesting Phoenix wanted to move Green for a more established playmaker.

"Everything I've heard is that the Suns are not shopping Jalen Green, and that they are not really in need and in search of a point guard," Fischer said.

For New Orleans, the timing isn't ideal.

Dejounte Murray Trade Request Faces New Complication

Murray formally requested a trade Friday, Nov. 13, with the Pelicans confirming that his representatives had informed the organization of his desire to leave.

The team said it would explore options to accommodate the request.

Phoenix quickly emerged as a possible destination.

According to The Athletic's Sam Amick , Murray has interest in joining the Suns, while his representatives have explored the possibility of a deal involving Green.

The potential swap appeared to offer both teams something different.

Phoenix would receive a veteran guard with extensive playmaking experience. New Orleans would acquire a younger scorer who could become part of its long-term plans.

However, reporting earlier this week indicated the teams had not engaged in formal discussions about such a trade.

Fischer's latest update raises further doubts.

"I am here to pour some cold water on Phoenix being the super active group right now," Fischer said.

Fischer explained that the Suns are still evaluating a roster that has undergone considerable changes.

Starting center Mark Williams has been unavailable, while Phoenix continues adjusting to new forward Miles Bridges.

The team also wants to determine whether Green and Devin Booker can develop a productive partnership.

Fischer emphasized that Green was someone Phoenix specifically targeted when it traded Kevin Durant to Houston.

"I have not gotten the sense that they are looking to move him anytime soon whatsoever," Fischer said.

That position could change if Phoenix's early-season struggles continue.

For now, though, there is little indication the Suns are preparing to part with Green.

Pelicans Must Explore Other Dejounte Murray Trade Options

Phoenix's reluctance doesn't eliminate the possibility of a Murray trade elsewhere.

The former All-Star remains under contract beyond this season through a player option, giving New Orleans time to evaluate potential offers rather than rush into a deal.

Still, Murray's public request has created an awkward situation for a franchise trying to establish stability.

The Pelicans have already acknowledged his desire to move on. They now must find a trade that makes sense for the organization.

The Suns' reported stance is another reminder that identifying an interested destination and completing a deal are two different things.

For Murray and New Orleans, the search continues.

articles.title: Vikings Get Big News on Key Defensive Starter
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell spoke with the media on Wednesday. He was able to deliver some positive news on some key players. This included lineb...
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell spoke with the media on Wednesday. He was able to deliver some positive news on some key players. This included linebacker Blake Cashman, who has been dealing with injuries over the past week

Cashman was in concussion protocol last week. He suffered the injury after suffering a concussion in week nine against the Buffalo Bills. He missed last week's game against the Green Bay Packers due to the concussion. Now, it appears that he could be in a spot to return for the team's game against the San Francisco 49ers.

O'Connell elaborated on this to the media on Wednesday afternoon per ESPN's Kevin Seifert.

Cashman's Return Would Be Huge Boost For Vikings

Cashman's return would certainly be welcome for the Vikings. He has been the defensive play-caller for the team this season. He has recorded 76 combined tackles, 4.5 sacks, seven passes defended, and a fumble recovery across eight games. Cashman has been a defensive leader for the team this season. In addition to getting Jordan Addison back for the stretch run, it appears that Cashman will have the opportunity to come back as well.

In addition to being a dependable veteran, he has been able to help the Vikings in other ways this season. Breaking it down even further, he has been a dependable pass-rusher. He has generated 16 total pressures in 19 by insects and quarterback hits on six pass-rush snaps. That aggressiveness has been a key hallmark of Brian Flores's defense. The aggressiveness itself shows in other ways as well. He has 76 tackles and shares the team lead in tackles for loss with Andrew Van Ginkel.

Vikings Defense Has Been Elite This Season

A Cashman return would set things up nicely for the Vikings as they look to make a key push during the playoff run. He has been a defensive anchor for a unit that is already extremely strong. They ranked first in the league in 14 points allowed per game. This breaks down to 226 points in total.

They have allowed 273.2 yards per game, which is second in the league. They have been stingy in terms of pass defense, as they have allowed 161.4 yards per game. That is good enough for second in the league. In addition, they have only allowed six passing touchdowns.

There is a bit of a drop-off in terms of their run defense. They have allowed 111.9 yards per game, which is 17 th in the league. However, they have only surrendered five rushing touchdowns, which is good enough for fourth in the entire league. Even in one of their weaker aspects of the defense, they still remain strong.

The pass rush aspect of the defense has been absolutely fantastic, as they have recorded 37 sacks this year. They are second in the league with 17 takeaways and second in the league with a +8 turnover differential. Simply put, they have been an absolute monster when it comes to the defensive side of football.

Getting Cashman back would certainly add to that. He has been a major part of what they have been able to do, and it has been fun to watch.

articles.title: Golf: LIV paid players millions as UK businesses owed thousands
articles.summary: A BBC Sport investigation has found bills to UK companies were already overdue when LIV Golf made its final payments to players and executives before filing for bankruptcy.
articles.body:
LIV Golf - backed by more than $5bn (£3.8bn) from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund - paid millions to players and executives in the weeks before filing for bankruptcy, while leaving a trail of unpaid bills from UK suppliers.

BBC Sport has seen invoices from five small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, all of which were overdue before LIV made its final payments to players.

Global Infusion Group, , external a Buckinghamshire company that provided catering at July's LIV Golf UK event, is still owed £321,671, due on 7 August.

Suffolk-based BD365 Clean , external provided 108 cleaning staff and is owed £75,225, most of which was due on 20 July and 13 August.

"It just feels completely immoral," said Bonnie May, chief executive of Global Infusion Group.

"It really matters to a business of our scale. The impact has been huge, both personally and professionally."

Only $2m (£1.5m) has been earmarked so far by the Saudi owners to pay unsecured creditors, leaving many smaller companies unsure if they will receive anything at all.

Yet court filings reveal LIV made 59 payments to golfers on 31 July, amounting to $16.6m (£12.6m) and matching prize money for the same LIV Golf UK event.

A further $34.2m (£25.9m) went to players between 17 August and 3 September following tournaments in New York and Indianapolis, including $6.4m (£4.9m) to 2026 champion Jon Rahm just five days before the bankruptcy filing.

Four senior LIV executives also received retention bonuses totalling nearly $3m (£2.3m) in August.

"It's sickening," said Krissi Foskett, owner of BD365 Clean, who described the unpaid bills as "almost an extinction-level event" for her team.

"How can they sleep at night, knowing they are potentially putting companies out of business?"

Meanwhile, public records list more than £3,000 owed to Goodysphere, , external a family-run Yorkshire firm that provides a sensory bus designed to help autistic children who may find busy events overwhelming.

LIV Golf did not respond to our request for comment.

However, in August, LIV chief executive Scott O'Neil said he hoped they would be able to pay their suppliers.

"What I would say to them is we're doing everything we can to make sure we can do right by them and the work they committed."

'It's Saudi money, that’s safe as houses'

The controversial breakaway league had been owned and bankrolled by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) since its launch season in 2022.

But in April, the fund announced it would end its backing after the 2026 season, putting LIV's future in doubt.

"Our understanding was that the funding would take LIV through 2026," said Global Infusion Group's May, whose company had about 60 staff catering for players and broadcasters.

"We weren't aware the funding had already stopped and there wasn't enough to actually fulfil their obligations."

PIF's multi-billion-dollar investment helped it to lure some of golf's biggest names and disrupt the PGA Tour's dominance of the sport.

"It's Saudi money, that's safe as houses, we thought," said Foskett.

"Their head honchos came along and enjoyed hospitality. We were there cleaning up at one o'clock in the morning then back in at five in the morning, only to be treated like this."

PIF remains the majority owner of Newcastle United, while Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 Fifa World Cup.

"I'm sure the country won't want to be saddled with the characterisation that it doesn't pay its bills," said professor Simon Chadwick, who is an expert in the business and politics of sport across Africa, Europe and Asia.

"I do find it surprising that they would simply walk away. I think they would want to engage in some kind of remedial action, particularly in terms of managing their image and reputation."

Filmmaker Joe Bentley spent eight days from April working on a video for LIV's YouTube channel that is still online.

He is owed nearly £6,000, with £2,226 due on 31 July.

The video was part of the 'LIV Back' series, set up to "focus on the impact LIV players and teams are making off the course".

He filmed at two schools taking part in 'Little Sticks', a LIV outreach programme which aimed to provide golf equipment and training in areas of deprivation.

"You feel massively deflated, a bit cheated and undervalued," said Bentley.

"Everyone I dealt with at LIV was lovely. The first email I sent chasing was to a production coordinator or a manager and even she was appalled that we hadn't been paid."

Gateshead Council is also owed £1,912, due on 22 August, relating to 'Little Sticks'.

"Transformation is not a short-term process," said Professor Chadwick.

"If you're going to embark on investment programmes in community sport, grassroots sport, you've got to make a long-term commitment and those changes have got to take place."

"The contacts we had sadly all lost their jobs," said Giles Mitchell, whose company, Office Pantry, supplied food to LIV's office on London's South Bank.

"We didn't hear anything from them and then their emails started bouncing back."

There was hope the competition could survive in some form with new investment, but in November LIV announced it was winding down operations.

In the bankruptcy filings, LIV estimated it had between $500m and $1bn (£380m-£760m) in liabilities and at least 1,000 creditors.

The largest 30 unsecured creditors alone were listed with claims of more than $64m (£49m).

"I think the message is loud and clear to somebody like me that, no, we're not going to get paid for any of this," said May.

"If anything did come our way, I'm thinking it's going to be pennies in the pound, nothing which will have any impact, or even cover our legal fees."

Fourteen golfers were among the published creditors with the 30 largest unsecured claims.

Rahm topped the list with a claim of $7.5m (£5.7m), which he agreed to give up as part of his deal to leave the league.

Bryson DeChambeau ($5.7m/£4.3m), Dustin Johnson ($5.5m/£4.2m), Cameron Smith ($4.8m/£3.6m) and Tyrrell Hatton ($3.4m/£2.6m) also featured.

IMG Media, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, and British golf YouTuber Rick Shiels were each listed with claims of more than $1m (£760,000) too.

Meanwhile, BBC Sport understands the R&A is owed about £500,000 for advice on sustainable maintenance of courses used by LIV.

A hearing is scheduled for January to consider the wind-down plan, but creditors may have to wait longer to find out how much they will get back.

"I've had nights just sat there in tears, thinking, what is the point," said BD365 Clean's Foskett.

"How much comes in will honestly depend on whether or not the business will still be going at the end of January.

articles.title: Tiger Woods: Fifteen-time major champion to design new links course in Northern Ireland
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is to design Northern Ireland's first new championship links golf course in more than a century.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods is to design Northern Ireland's first new championship links golf course in more than a century.

On Thursday, Woods and his course architecture firm TGR Design unveiled plans for Bellarena Golf Links on the Causeway Coast.

The course will be located on Northern Ireland's north-west coast, about 20 miles west of three-time Open Championship venue Royal Portrush.

Fifteen-time major champion Woods said the opportunity to create a new course in one of golf's most celebrated destinations was a special one.

"Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team," said Woods.

"We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it."

The development, a partnership between Galgorm Collection and US-based Reef Destinations, is expected to break ground in 2027, subject to planning approval, with a target opening date of July 2029.

"To have Tiger Woods and his company design a golf course in Northern Ireland is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, it's unbelievable," said Galgorm Collection chief executive Colin Johnston.

"It's bringing together fantastic companies and partners and creating something that will benefit Northern Ireland for many years to come."

Johnston said the dramatic setting was one of the key reasons the site stood out.

"The backdrop of Binevenagh Mountain and the views over Lough Foyle and into the Donegal hills are just stunning," he said.

The project could provide a boost to tourism in the north west.

"We know golf tourism is huge and we know it's close to capacity," Johnston said.

"If we want to bring more people to this part of the world, we need to increase that capacity, and it needs to be at the elite level people expect when they come here."

Johnston believes Bellarena can complement Northern Ireland's world-renowned venues such as Royal Portrush and Royal County Down.

"This is about bringing something new and exciting to this part of the world, bringing more people here and increasing tourism overall," he added.

Unlike some exclusive championship venues, Bellarena is expected to operate as a non-member, pay-and-play course.

TGR has designed courses in the United States but Bellarena will be the firm's first project in Europe.

articles.title: Tiger Woods: Former world No 1 hails 'special opportunity' to design new course in Northern Ireland with TGR Design
articles.summary: Bellarena will be TGR Design’s first course in Northern Ireland and the first new championship links to open in Northern Ireland in more than a century; TGR Design are a golf course design firm led by Tiger Woods
articles.body:
Reports linking the 15-time major champion with the proposed £30 million course at Bellarena on the north west coast between Limavady and Coleraine had been circulating for several weeks, ahead of Thursday's official announcement.

Hospitality group Galgorm Collection is building the course, with construction set to get under way next year if the required planning approvals are secured.

In a statement, Woods said: "Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team.

"We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it."

Galgorm Collection already owns and runs the championship parkland course at Galgorm Castle in Ballymena and a course at Roe Valley in Limavady, with plans to create an additional venue

Colin Johnston, chief executive of Galgorm Collection, announced that Woods and his TGR Design firm would craft the new links layout.

"Set against the spectacular backdrop of Northern Ireland's rugged northwest coast, our plans represent a once-in-a-generation opportunity to transform Northern Ireland's golfing and tourism future," Johnston said.

Bellarena is around 20 miles from Royal Portrush Golf Club, which hosted Shane Lowry's win at The Open in 2019 and Scottie Scheffler completing the third leg of the career Grand Slam in 2025.

Portstewart - host of Jon Rahm's win at the 2017 Irish Open - and Castlerock also boast acclaimed links courses in the region.

Reef Destinations has previously worked with TGR Design on course construction projects in the United States. Bellarena already has a historical link with the United States as a site of a US Army base during the Second World War.

Woods is poised to return to competitive golf next month for the first time in over two years after being confirmed as an entrant at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas from December 3-6.

The 50-year-old has not played competitively since The Open at Royal Troon in 2024 and has played limited golf since a career-threatening car crash in Florida in 2021.

Woods has had at least three different surgeries since his last start and spent time at a rehab facility in Switzerland earlier this year, having been arrested and charged with driving under the influence following a car crash near his home.

articles.title: Why Tiger Woods is preparing for an emotional PGA Tour comeback at the Hero World Challenge in 2026: Return details, injury recovery and what lies ahead for his golf future
articles.summary: Golf legend Tiger Woods announces his return to competitive play at the 2026 Hero World Challenge after overcoming injuries and personal challenges. Find out about his comeback plans and what it means for his future in the sport.
articles.body: Golf legend Tiger Woods is entering another major phase of his career as he begins his return to competitive play at the 2026 Hero World Challenge in December. The 15-time major champion has had a rough patch of injuries, surgeries, and personal issues that have kept him away from regular tournament play.Woods’ next event in the Bahamas will be key for him as it will give him a chance to test his competitive readiness against an international field. Fans of the game have been abuzz with his return, but there are still questions about how much he can play and whether another major challenge lies ahead.Details on Tiger Woods' confirmed Hero World Challenge returnWoods has confirmed that he will compete at the Hero World Challenge, scheduled for December 3–6, 2026, at Albany Golf Club in New Providence, Bahamas. The tournament marks his first individual competitive appearance since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut.It's an event Woods is well familiar with, running it through his TGR Foundation. He has won the competition five times, with his previous appearance coming in 2023, when he finished 18th.The 2026 edition will feature 20 golfers competing over 72 holes without a cut. Woods received one of the tournament's sponsor exemptions alongside Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler and defending champion Hideki Matsuyama are also among the notable names in the field.Why Tiger Woods' injury setbacks delayed comebackWoods' extended absence has largely been shaped by recurring physical problems. He tore his left Achilles in March 2025 and missed the rest of the season. He had a second back procedure in October 2025, adding to his long history of spinal surgeries.Then, on March 27, 2026, he was involved in a vehicle accident in Florida, and his recovery suffered another setback. Woods took time away from the game to focus on his health and treatment after the incident. In September, he pleaded no contest to reduced misdemeanor charges related to reckless driving and refusing to submit to a lawful test. His plea agreement included a five-year driver's license suspension.Despite these difficulties, Woods has offered encouraging updates about his physical condition. Speaking to SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio in November, he said he was feeling better and had been training regularly. His preparations suggest that he is working towards returning with improved fitness rather than rushing back into competition.What Tiger Woods' return means for the futureThe Hero World Challenge could help determine how much competitive golf Woods can manage moving forward. Walking the course and completing four rounds will be an important physical test after his Achilles injury and multiple back operations.His possible participation in the PNC Championship, scheduled for December 19–20, has also attracted attention. Woods has regularly competed in the father-son event alongside his son, Charlie Woods. However, their participation in the 2026 edition has not been confirmed.Another potential appearance is in the 2026–27 season of TGL, where Woods represents Jupiter Links Golf Club. The season is scheduled to begin on December 27, offering another opportunity for him to return to competitive golf in a different format.The bigger question concerns the 2027 major championships, particularly the Masters. Woods has not announced a complete competitive schedule, and his immediate priority will be determining how his body responds to tournament conditions. His return in the Bahamas is therefore an important first step, although it does not guarantee a full PGA Tour comeback or another major title challenge.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler announces a bold plan to follow PGA broadcasts in 2027, aiming to double viewership and secure the tour's future.
articles.body:
The LPGA Tour season concludes this weekend with the CME Group Tour Championship in Naples, Fla., offering a $4 million winner's check and a shot at the CME Globe title. articles.title: Stephen Sweeney Fixes Putt With Two Key Setup Tweaks
articles.summary: PGA Tour coach Stephen Sweeney corrects a golfer's putting stroke using two specific setup adjustments, a fix detailed in a new Yahoo Sports report.
articles.body:
Setup fundamentals often get overlooked by players chasing distance or power, yet they form the bedrock of consistency on the greens. A recent report from Yahoo Sports highlights how PGA Tour putting coach Stephen Sweeney corrected a struggling golfer's stroke using just two small adjustments. The lesson proved that a reliable setup allows a player to make fewer compensations during the actual stroke. When the eyes and hips align correctly, the putter face stays square, turning a miss into a make.

The golfer in the story arrived at the lesson expecting work on the stroke mechanics. Instead, Sweeney identified a fundamental flaw in the stance. "Where your eyes are right now, I tend to see if players' eyes are inside the ball line; they tend to look out to the right," Sweeney said. This misalignment caused the putter to move slightly on the inside on the backswing, even though it felt square to the player. The result was a subconscious aim to the right of the hole and a stroke path that moved from in to out.

Sweeney prescribed a "tabletop" setup to fix the eye position, similar to the stance used by Michelle Wie West during her prime. The coach instructed the player to hinge at the waist more aggressively. "As a general rule of thumb, I like to see a two putter head-(width) from the ball to the toe line," Sweeney said. The player then bends forward at the hips until the eyes sit directly over the golf ball. This simple shift in posture forces the putter to start back on a true path. "As the putter goes back, the putter is moving a little on the inside — but pretty square to where you aimed it," Sweeney noted. These changes eliminated the need for the player to manipulate the clubface during the stroke, leading to a more consistent roll.

The Value of Setup Over Stroke Mechanics

Most amateur golfers spend hours practicing their putting stroke, trying to fix the path or the face angle while standing up too tall. The report from Yahoo Sports illustrates that the stroke itself was not the problem. The issue lay in the setup. When the eyes are inside the ball, the brain forces the hands to manipulate the club to get it back on line. This creates a shaky stroke that lacks repeatability. By moving the eyes over the ball, the body naturally aligns the putter face. This approach removes the variable of hand manipulation, allowing the pendulum motion to work as intended.

Coaches like Sweeney often find that players who struggle on short putts have a setup that forces them to aim right to compensate for an inside-out path. Correcting the eye position fixes the aim and the path simultaneously. The "tabletop" feel creates a stable platform that supports the stroke. This method works for players of all skill levels, from beginners to professionals. The margin for error on the greens is so slim that even a small setup error can lead to a miss. Fixing the foundation allows the player to trust the stroke without overthinking the mechanics.

Putting is the only part of the game where power is rarely the goal. Consistency and touch drive the score. The adjustments detailed in the Yahoo Sports report show how a simple change in posture can yield immediate results. Instead, the player sets up correctly and lets the stroke happen. This shift in mindset is crucial for breaking through putting slumps. The data supports this: when the eyes are over the ball, the stroke becomes more repeatable. The putter stays on the intended line, and the ball rolls true.

Without a proper setup, no amount of stroke practice will fix the underlying alignment issues. The two adjustments—moving the eyes over the ball and adopting a tabletop stance—provide a clear path to improvement. Players who adopt these changes often find their putting confidence returns quickly.

articles.body:

We got the big penalty to get those guys down there. They've got a big-time field goal kicker. A couple of big plays, you know, in the first half, the two big plays were the ones that killed us there early. Got a pretty good grip on it after that. Kind of held it down after that. Usually, the finishes happen when you're able to generate those finishes with sacks, or you're able to get interceptions. You would like to be able to stop some of those plays and get off the grass at those moments. Then that score, when they got to where it was, those things didn't happen. We didn't execute that way. articles.title: LPGA Finally Gets Its PGA Tour Lead-In Strategy Right
articles.summary: LPGA Commissioner Craig Kessler outlines a bold plan to ride PGA Tour coattails, doubling weekend TV windows to finally give women's golf the exposure it des...
articles.body:
The LPGA is finally stopping the guessing game and riding the coattails of the men's tour. On Wednesday, Commissioner Craig Kessler announced a clear strategy to piggyback on PGA Tour broadcasts, aiming to keep fans glued to their screens when the men finish their rounds. This is not a vague promise of "more exposure" but a concrete deal with TV partners to shift the schedule. The move targets the exact problem that has plagued the tour for decades: nobody is watching because nobody knows the women are playing.

For years, the LPGA asked fans to hunt for coverage or wait for tape delays that never came. That era ends now. According to Sports Business Journal , Kessler "outlined a plan negotiated with the tour's TV partners to allow for more LPGA events to follow PGA Tour broadcasts." If a viewer stays for the men's final group, they are already there for the women. Kessler told reporters that PGA Tour fans "will be inclined to leave their sets on and roll into LPGA coverage." It is a basic retention play that should have happened twenty years ago.

Next year, CBS or NBC will broadcast at least eight weekend slots for the LPGA immediately after PGA Tour events. Yahoo Sports reported this figure represents a doubling of this season's total. More time on broadcast networks means more eyes, not just more hours on cable. Kessler noted that "We're working to make sure we follow PGA Tour coverage because we benefit from their lead-in." The tour is finally admitting that it needs the men's momentum to survive.

The CME Group Tour Championship concludes the 2026 season with an $11 million purse, offering a massive $4 million top prize to the winner. Yet, the business side remains shaky. CME Group CEO Terry Duffy told CNBC on Wednesday that his company has "not come to a conclusion yet" about extending its title sponsorship beyond 2027. Duffy will step down on March 1, 2027, leaving the future of the tour's biggest event in limbo.

The LPGA is betting that visibility will solve the sponsorship puzzle. Kessler believes that "We're all after the same goal, which is growing the game and providing more exposure to people around the world, and that lends itself to collaboration." The tour is leveraging its relationship with the PGA Tour to secure these slots, even though the LPGA receives only a small percentage of the rights fee revenue. The gamble is that a larger audience will attract bigger sponsors to replace the uncertainty around the CME deal.

Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand aims for her third straight win at the championship, heading a 60-player field at Tiburon Golf Club. She has won four times this year and knows the course well. "This course wasn't that hard," Jeeno said on Wednesday. "Hard to not be able to be aggressive on it." Her aggressive style fits the new broadcast window perfectly, offering drama when the cameras roll.

Nelly Korda also headlines the field with four titles in 2026, including her fourth major crown at the U.S. Women's Open. The U.S. Women's Open drew an average audience of 1.3 million on NBC, peaking at 2.1 million viewers. Korda's consistency proves the product is ready for prime time. The LPGA now just needs the TV partners to keep the switch on. With the 2026 season marking the first instance of zero tape delays for the LPGA, every round guaranteed some live coverage. Golf Channel will air the inaugural Nanea Cup in primetime right after the PGA Tour's Players Championship concludes its third and final rounds on the weekend.

articles.title: Brooks Koepka’s PGA Tour Return Falls Short Of Expectations
articles.summary: Brooks Koepka calls his PGA Tour comeback a disappointment as he seeks to revive his Ryder Cup hopes with putting help.
articles.body:
Brooks Koepka's return to the PGA Tour has not matched the high expectations set for a five-time major champion. The golfer who once dominated the world stage now faces a steep climb to regain his form. While the tour itself has evolved into a more competitive environment, Koepka's personal results suggest a significant struggle.

The tour has changed since Koepka first departed. According to Inquirer.com, the landscape shifted after LIV Golf ceased operations, leaving a vacuum that the PGA Tour filled with increased prize money and a streamlined structure. Tiger Woods noted this shift, stating, "I can confidently say the PGA Tour is in the best position it has ever been." The financial incentives have grown, with total prize money almost doubling as the tour adopted a merit-based product, yet Koepka has not capitalized on these opportunities.

The competition Koepka faces is stronger than in previous years, driven by players like Scottie Scheffler. Scheffler's dominance in 2024 was acknowledged by Koepka while he was still playing on LIV Golf. "Scottie had a hell of a year," Koepka admitted in comments reported by Yahoo Sports . Scheffler's performance that season was historic, playing 19 events and recording seven wins. He made all 19 cuts and achieved 12 top-5 finishes. His peers' level of consistency raises the bar for anyone looking to return to the top of the standings.

Koepka suggested that the competitive landscape would have been different had he and other LIV players remained on the PGA Tour. He noted that while Scheffler would have won many tournaments, the LIV contingent "would have put up a good fight." This sentiment highlights the depth of talent that left the tour and the challenge of re-entering a field that has since adapted and improved. The absence of these players during the peak of Scheffler's run allowed the American to accumulate victories, but their return or the return of others like Koepka introduces a new dynamic of resistance.

Financial stakes have also risen, with players like Jordan Spieth acknowledging the ripple effect of the massive purse increases. Spieth admitted, "I would be lying if I said that we would have gone through this without LIV," referencing the financial boost that came from the rival tour's spending. This increase in prize money means that every tournament carries more weight, adding pressure to perform. For a player like Koepka, who thrives under pressure, the environment is theoretically ideal, yet the results have not reflected that potential.

The question now is whether a putting specialist can help Koepka regain his form and secure a spot in the Ryder Cup. The current trajectory suggests that without a significant adjustment in his short game, his chances remain slim. The tour is in a better position than ever, but that does not guarantee success for individual players who have been away from the regular competition for an extended period. The gap in performance must be closed through specific technical improvements and a return to the mental toughness that defined his earlier career.

Koepka's ability to adapt to the current tour conditions will determine his future standing. The data from 2024 shows that the field is deeper and more consistent than ever before. With Scheffler winning The Masters and racking up multiple top-10 finishes in other majors, the margin for error has shrunk. Koepka must find a way to compete against this new standard of excellence. The Ryder Cup push depends on immediate results, and the window to prove his relevance is narrowing.

The focus now turns to whether a putting guru can spark the necessary turnaround. Koepka's return has been a disappointment so far, and the next few tournaments will define whether he can reclaim his status as a top contender in the game.
